articleTitle: Radar-Lidar Fusion for Classification of Traffic Signaling Motion in Automotive Applications
abstract: Advanced driver-assisted system (ADAS) uses multiple sensors such as Radar, Lidar, or Cameras in vehicles to create a robust perception against challenging weather conditions and individual sensor failures. In typical conditions, Lidar and Camera can perceive the surrounding much better than the radar whereas, under low light or extreme weather conditions (fog, rain, snow) the radar outperforms both as it works independently of light source. These sensors in the ADAS system help to minimize driving errors by providing necessary information to the driver or taking automatic actions based on what it perceives. However, in some unstructured environments, which do not have any operational traffic lights present, a person via appropriate gesturing directs the traffic. The task of autonomous vehicles recognizing human body language and gestures in traffic-directing scenarios is significantly difficult. To overcome this challenge, based on the US traffic system, we present a new dataset collected of traffic signaling motions using millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar, camera, Lidar, and motion-capture system. Initial classification results from Radar microDoppler ($\mu$-D) signature and Lidar data analysis using Multimodal Neural Network demonstrate that sensor fusion can not only very accurately (around 98%) classify traffic signaling motions in automotive applications but also outperforms the radar-based and lidar-based classification by around 7% and 4% respectively.

articleTitle: Clutter Modeling and Analysis for Bistatic Space-Based Early Warning Radar with GEO Transmitter and LEO Receiver
abstract: This paper presents a study on the bistatic space-based early warning radar system, a novel concept of space-based radar in which the transmitter and receiver are mounted on a geosynchronous orbit satellite and a low Earth orbit satellite, respectively. A mathematical model is proposed to accurately describe the clutter distribution by analyzing the geometric relationship of the bistatic system and taking into account the effect of Earth’s rotation. Then the clutter distribution trajectories are given, which present the severe non-stationarity. Simulation analysis are performed to investigate the impact of system antenna pattern and actual beam illuminating range on clutter power spectrum. Finally, the signal-to-clutter-plus-noise ratio loss of three-dimensional space-time adaptive processing (3D-STAP) method for different spatial degrees of freedom is analyzed. This paper can provide references for the study of bistatic space-based early warning radar.

articleTitle: Harbour Area Change Detection and Analysis Using SAR Images from a Recent Measurement Campaign
abstract: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) data are widely used for remote sensing applications, such as change detection and environmental monitoring. This paper presents a recent measurement campaign for SAR images using the LORA system and investigates the applicability of the collected data for change detection. The region of interest in this study is a busy commercial harbour area in the south of Sweden. During the measurements, there were significant changes on the ground in the parking lot as trucks were disembarking a ship. The obtained SAR images were first filtered to have similar regions of interest in the Fourier domain to increase the coherence magnitude. Then, a constant false alarm rate (CFAR) algorithm was employed to detect changes with respect to trucks. In addition, optical aerial images were collected during this measurement campaign and were utilized to adjust the CFAR detection threshold. As a result, all the changed and unchanged regions corresponding to the selected targets were detected successfully. Moreover, a pattern of trucks’ utilization of the harbour’s parking lot during this peak time was obtained. The results demonstrate the applicability of the data from the ongoing measurement campaign and the possibility of further algorithm development for target detection and classification.

articleTitle: Automatic LPI Radar Waveform Recognition Using Vision Transformer
abstract: This paper investigates the classification of low probability of intercept (LPI) radar signals by exploiting the intrinsic advantages of the Vision Transformer (ViT). Due to the characteristics of LPI radar signals, such as intrapulse modulation, wide frequency bands, and low transmission power, these signals are challenging to be detected and classified using traditional analytic methods. This has led to the adoption of various deep learning techniques to overcome these limitations. On the one hand, the ViT, originally developed for natural language processing, has demonstrated outstanding performance in computer vision by replacing the structure of the convolutional neural network (CNN) with the transformer, specifically leveraging self-attention. Therefore, this paper explores a method based on the ViT technique for classifying LPI signal images. The simulation results show that the proposed ViT method outperforms the traditional CNN method by 12.8% at −10dB SNR.

articleTitle: UAS-borne CWSF SAR imaging: evaluation and compensation of Doppler effect
abstract: Radar sensors based on Unmanned Aerial Systems (UAS) poses new challenges in the field of data processing. The fine compensation of Doppler effect is one of this, especially for continuous wave step-frequency (CWSF) radar that typically operates at low pulse repetition frequency (PRF). In this paper the implications of Doppler effect on synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging are theoretically investigated and a specific focusing algorithm is proposed. Experimental data, acquired in a controlled but realistic scenario, validate the method.

articleTitle: Passive Multistatic Localization of Space Objects using LOFAR Radio Telescope
abstract: The paper presents the idea and results of the experimental trials devoted to passive multistatic observation of space objects in low-Earth orbits employing an astronomical LOFAR (LOw-Frequency ARray) radio telescope as a surveillance receiver. Terrestrial commercial digital radio transmitters operating in the VHF band were used as illuminators of opportunity. The large antenna array of the LOFAR radio telescope allows us to record relatively weak echo signals reflected from space objects. Reference signals were acquired by software-defined radio receivers located near illuminators of opportunity. Combining the results of bistatic measurements from three pairs of illuminator-receiver, we estimated the position of a space object in a Cartesian coordinate system. The results of the experiments confirm the possibility of determination of the space object’s position utilizing the passive radar system using antenna arrays such as the array in the LOFAR radio telescopes and the commercial terrestrial transmitters as illuminators of opportunity.

articleTitle: Parameters Extraction of Unknown Radar Signals Using Change Point Detection
abstract: Severa1 applications like seismic data processing or system monitoring require detecting abrupt changes. This paper considers the problem of signal detection and recognition in the context of radar application applied to the segmentation of an unknown received signal. Therefore, a well known change point detection algorithm is implemented, the Cumulative Sum algorithm (CuSum), to detect and extract signals of interest in radar recordings. It enables the localization of the onset and end of unknown waveforms in a pulse train, making its extraction from a noisy background and its characterisation possible. Different models of the problems are considered and compared. The capacity of the algorithm to correctly retrieve the temporal parameters of a signal is tested on both simulations and acquisitions.

articleTitle: Effects of Range Doppler-rate Coupling on High Frequency Chirp Radar for Accelerating Targets
abstract: Range Doppler coupling is a range bias resulting from the use of linear frequency modulated waveforms. This coupling impacts radar returns of highly accelerating targets resulting in apparent range walk across a processing interval. Because of this, methods for detecting fast objects with long integration times introduce unwanted artefacts to chirp radars utilising low bandwidths and low repetition frequencies. This paper details that in addition to the range bias, range Doppler coupling artefacts impact higher order measurements, and also describes how these affects can be mitigated. Results of radar returns from satellites demonstrating sensitivity improvements are included, illustrating that mitigating range Doppler-rate coupling will benefit any time-frequency method attempting accelerating target detection.

articleTitle: Classification of polarimetric SAR imagery based on improved MRF model using Wishart distance and category confidence-degree
abstract: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) image classification using convolutional neural networks (CNN) has achieved great performance in military and civil fields. However, spatial semantic information is often not fully considered for SAR image classification, which lead to the misclassification of edge regions. To address this issue, an improved Markov random field (MRF) model using Wishart distance and category confidence-degree for polarimetric SAR data interpretation is introduced by combining polarimetric features with spatial information of SAR image. Firstly, polarimetric features in the rotation domain are extracted from SAR image. Secondly, the preliminary classification result and category confidence-degree are obtained by using support vector machine (SVM) classifier. Thirdly, the classification category is updated by the proposed MRF model using Wishart distance and category confidence-degree. Experimental results on real datasets show that the overall classification accuracy of the proposed method is much higher than the other conventional algorithm.

articleTitle: Human Target Recognition Using MIMO FMCW Radar and Slow-time DC-Value Suppression
abstract: Frequency-modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radars provide distinct movement-based features that aid with remote human target identification. A 2D complex-valued range-angle image (RAI) is produced by applying a 2D fast Fourier transform (FFT) to fast-time samples of virtual receiver array generated by the time-division multiplexing (TDM) concept. Unlike the human chest wall, which produces a significant phase shift from one chirp to the next in FMCW radar, stationary clutters exhibit an approximately constant phase during the coherent processing interval (CPI). This paper employs an advanced 77-GHz multiple-input and multiple-output (MIMO) FMCW radar. It applies a DC-value suppression technique along the slow-time axis to develop a stationary-clutter-free RAI for human target identification. The main advantage of this approach is its high precision and low computational complexity for real-time applications. In comparison with analogous research works, a significant reduction of approximately 58% in the average execution time is observed. The conducted experiments and robust graphical representations demonstrate the applicability of the proposed method in a complex, congested environment.

articleTitle: Mapping Flood Events Across Australia using NovaSAR-1 and Sentinel-1
abstract: It is important to be able to rapidly identify inundation extent during hazardous flood events. Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) remote sensing technologies enable regional-scale identification of inundation, without being affected by cloud cover. This study compares flood extent as derived from C-band Sentinel-1 and S-band NovaSAR-1 for both co-polarised and cross-polarised bands. The results are validated using a water map derived from a cloud-free Sentinel-2 image acquired at a similar date to the SAR data. The results show that the cross-polarised bands provide a more accurate estimate of flood extent (based on their F1-scores), while the NovaSAR-1 HH band had a much-reduced estimate of flood extent. The cross-polarised bands from both Sentinel-1 and NovaSAR-1 were then used to identify ephemeral lakes as well as follow a floods progression along a floodplain.

articleTitle: Improved Multi-Person Vital Signs Estimation Algorithm in Sitting and Standing Positions using MIMO FMCW Radar
abstract: The use of FMCW radars for non-contact monitoring of vital signs has gained an increased attention in the healthcare sector within the past few years. In this paper, we propose an improved contactless vital signs estimation algorithm that is capable of detecting multiple persons, both in sitting and standing positions, and accurately estimating their respiratory and heart rates. The proposed algorithm combines several state-of-the-art radar vital signs estimation approaches, including empirical mode decomposition with principal component analysis, density-based clustering, and Kalman filtering. The proposed algorithm was developed and tested using a market-available FMCW radar in MIMO configuration. The testing results showed that the algorithm can estimate the respiratory and heart rates with an error of 0.7 cycles/minute and 2.3 beats/minute, respectively.

articleTitle: Resolving Target Ambiguities in Automotive Radar Using DDMA Techniques
abstract: Doppler division multiple access (DDMA) is a slow-time phase coding technique that enables implementing multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar using legacy phased-array hardware. However, DDMA is well known to cause ambiguity in the received Doppler spectrum. Although asymmetric DDMA has been proposed to mitigate the target ambiguity problem, it can result in collisions between different target reflections associated with different transmit antennas. In this paper, we introduce a method for resolving target ambiguities in DDMA-based automotive MIMO radar. The proposed method utilizes conventional DDMA with all transmit antennas except one. Simultaneously, a single slow-time channel that is independent from the DDMA code is used to resolve the target ambiguities. It is shown that the proposed system achieves an effective solution with little additional complexity with respect to the standard DDMA technique. Simulation examples are used to demonstrate the performance of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Design of a Multilayer Longitudinally Compact UWB 3-dB Microwave Coupler using Multiple Apertures
abstract: Miniaturization of 3-dB couplers in transverse direction (width) has been greatly discussed in the literature while little to no information is available on reducing the coupler length. This is because of the trade-off between coupler length and bandwidth. A wideband coupler can be designed using the conventional Bethe-Hole theory which suggests adding multiple apertures in the longitudinal direction, thus increasing the device length. Another factor is aperture size which determines the coupling strength and puts additional strain on compactness of a 3-dB coupler. Contrariwise, this paper proposes to merge two weak (and hence compact) coupling mechanisms to design a wideband 3-dB coupler. This is achieved by using a longitudinal rectangular slot and three cross-slots in the transverse direction. Because of weak coupling, the slot sizes are smaller than a conventional 3-dB coupler, hence yielding a device whose length is less than one guided wavelength ($\lambda_{g}$) without compromising on the bandwidth. The presented coupler is 0.63$\lambda_{g}$ in length which is smaller than the state-of-the-art while maintaining a fractional bandwidth of 37.7% which is comparable to Half-Mode Substrate Integrated Waveguide (HMSIW) couplers.

articleTitle: Privacy-Preserving Speaker Recognition Using Radars for Context Estimation in Future Multi-Modal Hearing Assistive Technologies
abstract: Speaker recognition (SR) from speech can help determine the environmental context in multi-talker conversational scenarios to enable the design of context-aware multi-modal hearing assistive technology. In this paper, we argue that the use of wireless sensors such as radars can offer many benefits over conventional audio and visual sensors, such as not being afflicted by privacy and environmental issues, e.g., improper lighting, environmental noise, and potential security concerns of audio and video channels. Radar is relatively less explored and has many advantages over other contactless approaches, such as being more compact compared to RFID and having a better range and resolution than ultrasound and microwave sensors. To this end, we propose the use of ultrawideband radar coupled with a deep learning model for SR from silent speech to enable the design of future context-aware multimodal hearing assistive technology. We collected a dataset from five individuals with origins in Europe, Asia, and the United Kingdom. We obtained an average performance of approximately 82% in recognising an unknown person from a set of known people. This demonstrates that the radar has good potential to be used for privacy-preserving SR in multi-talker environments where audio-visual and other contactless techniques have limited capabilities.

articleTitle: Hybrid Polarimetry Inverse SAR
abstract: The Inverse Synthetic Aperture Radar (ISAR) exploits the movement of the target to form high-resolution imaging of the target. Further, the multi-polarization acquisition in ISAR gathers additional information on the target’s scattering properties and surface characteristics that help to enhance the imaging capabilities of ISAR. In this manuscript, we suggest a novel multi-polarization ISAR configuration based on the Circular Transmit and Linear Receive (CTLR) combination, namely hybrid-pol ISAR, for the application of non-cooperative target detection and imaging. Hybrid-pol ISAR can capture sufficient information about the targets to characterize them properly, and simultaneously overcomes the demerits of full-polarimetric (full-pol) ISAR associated with the transmission of two pulses to capture a single unit of polarimetric back-scattered information. The real Tank-72 ISAR data is implemented for the validation, which was captured under the MSTAR program by Georgia Technology Research Institute (GTRI).

articleTitle: Velocity Ambiguity Resolution using Opposite Chirprates with LFM Radar
abstract: High frequency radar observations of satellites are altered by the impacts of range Doppler coupling along with ambiguous Doppler measurements, making the estimation of true range and velocity challenging. This paper investigates the use of combining two coincident detections, from independent chirp transmitters, to instantaneously estimate target parameters. It shows the estimates produced are greatly improved with using chirprates with opposite polarity, even if the two transmit frequencies are closely spaced. The paper includes example results from an opportunistic pass of the International Space Station during a recent trial.

articleTitle: Mean Squared Error Analysis of Least Squares Envelope Fitting DoA Estimator
abstract: Least squares envelope fitting is a straightforward method of direction of arrival estimation that can be used in systems that employ scanning, either mechanical or electronic, to estimate angle. However, when viewed as a maximum likelihood estimator, it becomes clear the approach is based on somewhat unrealistic assumptions regarding the distribution of observations. In this paper, the impact of data distribution on bias and variance of this estimator is studied using analytic approach. Computer simulation experiments, performed for Rice and Rayleigh distributions, confirm high accuracy of the proposed analytic approach.

articleTitle: Amplitude Distribution of Low Grazing Angle G-band Littoral Sea Clutter
abstract: G-band radar sensing of the marine environment is of interest for maritime autonomy, however at present, no phenomenological data of low grazing angle sea clutter at this frequency is available in the literature. Future sensor design is contingent on the modeling of empirical data, with polarization expected to be a key parameter. This paper presents the results of an analysis of data of radar returns from the water’s surface gathered in 2022 at Coniston Water, UK. The difference in amplitude distribution and normalized radar cross section (NRCS) between HH (horizontal-horizontal) and VV (vertical-vertical) polarization is shown for two $0.5^{\mathrm{o}}$ wide grazing angle swaths centered at $2^{\mathrm{o}}$ and $4^{\mathrm{o}}$. HH is seen to produce longer-tailed distributions than VV for both swaths, with a mean NRCS for thresholded data (i.e. for wave signal peaks) of −33.3dB (HH) and −35.2dB (VV) for the swath centered at $2^{\mathrm{o}}$, and −38.6dB (HH) and −41.6dB (VV) for the swath centered at $4^{\mathrm{o}}$.

articleTitle: Clutter Compensation for Space-Air Bistatic Radar Based on Unitary Subspace Transformation
abstract: Since the space-air bistatic radar (SABR) system works in down-looking mode, it encounters a severely broadened clutter spectrum and the clutter is range dependent. Thereby diminishing the performance of space-time adaptive processing (STAP) technology through covariance matrix estimation error. It is necessary to perform clutter compensation before STAP clutter suppression. Inspired by the thinking of coherent signal subspace method for estimating the directions of arrival of wideband signals, we propose the range dependence compensation method which transforms the clutter subspace of training samples into the clutter subspace of reference range bin by unitary matrix transformation. Simulation examples are conducted to validate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Discrimination of small targets in sea clutter using a hybrid CNN-LSTM network
abstract: Reliable and robust radar target detection is a challenging task in the maritime environment, particularly as bright returns or sea spikes share many similarities with true targets and can be difficult to distinguish. One approach to overcome this challenge is to exploit the persistence of the target and consider detection as a basic classification problem, i.e. either a target is present or absent. In this work, discrimination of small fluctuating targets in sea clutter is demonstrated using a hybrid convolutional neural network with long short-term memory (CNN-LSTM). The proposed approach is able to distinguish targets by exploiting amplitude fluctuations over time, with improved classification observed as longer sequences of data are processed.

articleTitle: Hierarchical Classification of ISAR Sequences
abstract: Inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) is a common radar imaging technique used to characterise and classify non-cooperative targets. A number of different classification approaches have been proposed including the traditional approach which utilises geometric features extracted from images of known targets and more recently deep learning approaches. Hierarchical classification is designed to deal with large scale classification problems when there is a large number of targets. In this paper, a number of convolutional neural networks are compared to determine the best approach for hierarchical ship classification. Recent work on transfer learning, recurrent neural networks, and hierarchical structures are explored with the goal to find the best network design in terms of computational efficiency and classification accuracy.

articleTitle: iFURTHER Project - A Cognitive Network of HF Radars for Europe Defence
abstract: This paper presents the European project named iFURTHER that focuses on multi-site HF-OTH-R approaches. Facing the new military threats, the European Union seeks to develop disruptive defence systems that benefit from a new robust capability to complement existing surveillance systems. The iFURTHER project conceptualises the idea of a cognitive network of HF radars over Europe that provides the capabilities of large area surveillance and early warning to protect the EU.

articleTitle: Deep Sparse Array Design for Integrated Sensing and Communications
abstract: Sparse arrays are widely used to save area/power consumption and efficiently utilize hardware resources in sensing and communications applications. In this paper, we focus on sparse array design for integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) that is envisioned as one of the key technologies for future wireless networks for providing joint/shared access to the spectrum and reducing hardware costs. In particular, we consider a massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) ISAC array, for which hybrid mixed analog/digital beamforming is employed. We propose partitioning the consecutively-placed antennas into smaller subarrays thereby significantly reducing the number of possible sparse array configurations. Then, we introduce modeland learning-based methods to jointly solve the sparse array design and ISAC hybrid beamforming problems. Our numerical experiments show that the proposed approach significantly reduces the computational complexity while maintaining reasonable spectral efficiency.

articleTitle: A MIMO ISAR Approach with Depth Camera Motion Tracking for Improved Imaging in Walk-Through Security Scanners
abstract: Microwave security screening systems detect threats based on reconstructed radar images. Hence, aiming for the best possible reconstruction results is the main target for every personnel screening system. We introduce in this paper a computationally efficient imaging algorithm, that improves the imaging results for walk-through scanner systems notably by using an additional depth camera. To achieve this, body parts of a passing human are automatically detected and tracked in the recorded depth frames. The determined trajectory is then used to create an inverse synthetic aperture, resulting in a better target illumination and image resolution. Additionally, clutter and noise are reduced compared to a single reconstructed frame. Realistic measurements with a multiple input multiple output (MIMO) array, real human motions and different threat objects confirm the functionality and advantage of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: An Autonomous Approach to Deinterleave and Recover Radar Pulse Sequences in an Unknown Maritime Environment
abstract: In a high-density maritime environment, the recovery of radar pulse sequences presents a challenge for transponders due to interleaved pulses. Furthermore, because only a few manufacturers produce civil radars, the lack of diversity in signal signatures makes the task more difficult. In this paper, we introduce a new approach to deinterleave radar pulse sequences without requiring specific knowledge. Our proposed solution, based on a three-step approach, enables transponders to recognize their environment and interact with emitters more effectively without any training step. The effectiveness of this approach is demonstrated through simulations. The obtained results show that predicted clusters have a homogeneity score higher than 98%, a completeness score higher than 92%, and a Rand index higher than 97%. Our solution can deinterleave and recover radar pulse sequences in an unknown maritime environment in real-time without prior knowledge, while providing a thorough interpretation of results

articleTitle: Clutter Rank Estimation for Airborne Frequency Diversity Array Radar under Range Ambiguity
abstract: Space-time adaptive processing (STAP) with frequency diversity array (FDA) has shown superior advantages for handling range ambiguous clutter in airborne radar system. As an important concept of FDA-STAP, the clutter rank plays a fundamental role for the development of FDA-STAP algorithms. The existing techniques often estimate the clutter rank according to the subspace transformation matrix formulated from the transmit-receive steering vectors of any clutter echo. However, the real clutter echo depends on the transmit-time-receive steering vectors. This will lead to incorrect clutter rank estimation because the influence of time steering vector is ignored. In this paper, we study the formulation of subspace transformation matrix in transmit-time-receive domain. With the proposed subspace transformation matrix, the clutter rank can be accurately derived, which overcomes the shortcomings in transmit-receive domain. Furthermore, the maximum resolvable number of range ambiguity is derived, which is larger than that in transmit-receive domain. Numerical results confirm the accuracy of the derived clutter rank and the maximum resolvable number of range ambiguities.

articleTitle: GNSS-Based Non-Cooperative Air Traffic Situational Awareness
abstract: This work performs an initial feasibility assessment of a global navigation satellite system (GNSS)-based passive multistatic radar approach meant to enable non-cooperative air traffic situational awareness. First, the theoretical detection performance when assuming a long integration time is evaluated for both the bistatic and multistatic radar cases. Following this, the range and Doppler migration compensation approach needed to enable a high processing gain in practice is addressed and a multi-frame hybrid integration technique proposed. This approach builds up on our previous single frame long integration technique, corrects for the intra- and inter-frame range and Doppler migration components while allowing for different accelerations in each frame, therefore accounting for a geometry-induced relative jerk. Preliminary simulation results show the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Time Delay Compensation For Cascaded MIMO Radar With Injection-Locked Structure
abstract: Multi-level cascaded multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar plays a vital role in 4D radar imaging. However, addressing the phase mismatch in monolithic microwave integrated circuits (MMICs) remains a significant challenge. In MIMO radar with injection-locked structure, phase difference primarily arise from time delay in interconnections between MMICs. Currently, phase compensation methods in injection-locked feedthrough MIMO radar can be classified into hardware and software. However, existing software compensation methods lack sufficient accuracy, particularly in the millimeter-wave band above 70 GHz, where errors introduced by these methods result in high angular sidelobes. This paper proposes a novel software compensation method that achieves more accurate delay compensation, significantly reducing angular sidelobes and improving angle estimation accuracy.

articleTitle: Vehicles Detection, Tracking, and Classification Using 35GHz FMCW Radar
abstract: This paper introduces a new vehicle detection, tracking, and classification system that utilizes a 35 GHz FMCW radar. The system incorporates a monolithic microwave integrated circuit to replace traditional transmitting and receiving components, which reduces the size, power consumption, and overall cost of the radar. Additionally, a phase-locked loop frequency synthesis scheme is used to further optimize the system. The result is a cost-effective radar system that costs less than ten dollars. This paper not only explores a wide range of vehicle detection, tracking, and classification algorithms, but also optimizes them to run seamlessly on micro-controllers with low power consumption, low computational complexity, and low cost. This radar is capable of measuring the speed, distance, and traffic volume of multiple vehicles simultaneously - making it a versatile and valuable addition to any traffic monitoring system.

articleTitle: HFSWR Clutter Recognition Based on Attention DCNN
abstract: High frequency surface wave radar (HFSWR) suffers from passive interference caused by ionospheric clutter. Ionospheric clutter has a chaotic nature that makes a priori information insufficient for clutter suppression algorithms. In recent years, various clutter recognition methods for suppression have been proposed, including machine learning methods such as SVM, CNNs, and LSTM. However, existing models still have poor generalization performance and struggle to sustain high multi-class recognition accuracy in a realistic, time-varying, and highly complex ionospheric clutter environment. To address this issue, this paper proposes a deep learning ionospheric clutter recognition model with expansive convolutional networks. The model replaces the traditional convolutional-full-connected network with a modified dilated convolutional network with attention mechanism (AM-DCNN) to improve feature resolution and sample size requirements while maintaining recognition accuracy. The proposed method achieves high accuracy in recognizing five refinement characteristics of strong ionospheric clutter.

articleTitle: A Modular Conformal Antenna Array for Wide-Beam SAR and DAA Radars
abstract: A novel modular conformal antenna array structure is proposed in this paper that can provide a variable and wide field of view. The wide field of view is achieved through innovative conformal design while modularity ensures the scaling of field of view. Modularity is obtained by employing a subarray approach. An example prototype is presented for the applications of Detect & Avoid and Synthetic Aperture radars. The frequency of operation for this radar is 15.4 to 17.3 GHz. An individual subarray has 2x4 corner truncated patch elements to obtain the desired beamwidth in azimuth (45° – 65°) and elevation (20° – 30°) while corner truncation ensures circular polarisation over the entire band of DAA operation. These subarrays are then integrated into a conformal shape to obtain desired radiation characteristics.

Author Keywords: Reduction of Sidelobes and Grating lobes

articleTitle: High-Resolution 2D MIMO Radars for Traffic Gesture Recognition
abstract: Autonomous driving places high demands on auto-motive sensor suites in terms of environmental perception. This includes radar sensors, which must offer ever better imaging performance. As a consequence, imaging radars with large apertures and 2D beamforming capabilities with high-angular resolutions have emerged in recent years. On the algorithm side, these sensors open up new possibilities for deep learning-based environmental perception. Hence, this paper explores radar-based traffic gesture recognition with a 192-channel radar sensor with a large virtual aperture. The sparse array has an angular resolution of 1.45° and 6.17° in azimuth and elevation, respectively, which provides accurate and detailed radar point clouds. Subsequently, a convolutional neural network (CNN) for spectrogram-based classification and a PointNet-based model (PointNet+LSTM) for direct point cloud processing are trained on a traffic gesture dataset with 20 participants. PointNet+LSTM reaches a single-sensor accuracy of 90.8 % with pretraining from simulation data, demonstrating the great potential of radars with high angular resolution for reliable gesture recognition.

articleTitle: A NLOS Target Detection Method with MMW Radar under Low SNR
abstract: Due to the complexity of urban building environments and the reduced signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of electromagnetic (EM) waves after multiple reflections, it is difficult to detect targets in urban environments using the reflection of EM waves. At this time, if the target is detected based on detection before tracking (DBT), it is more likely to cause a false alarm or missed detection. Inspired by the idea of joint multi-frame accumulation detection targets in tracking before detection (TBD), we propose a new detection method for the NLOS target. Compared to DBT, this method ensures the detection probability of the target at low SNR while reducing the false alarm probability by judging the accumulated results of multiple frames. Furthermore, several experimental results show that when the target is behind a building corner, the algorithm can effectively reduce the generation of false targets while ensuring the probability of target detection.

articleTitle: SINR and WPSL Performance Analysis for Frequency Sparse Waveform
abstract: Frequency sparse waveform must be ensured to have interference immunity and low autocorrelation function (ACF) sidelobe level. In this study, we use the signal to interference plus noise ratio (SINR) and the weighted peak sidelobe level (WPSL) to represent the above two waveform properties, considering the minimization of SINR and WPSL under spectral and energy constraints to establish the optimization problem, proving that the problem is convex and solve for the optimal power spectral density (PSD) using the optimization toolbox. This study allows us to analyze the trade-off between SINR and WPSL and evaluate the band availability to select the best band.

articleTitle: Micro-Doppler Power Analysis for Drone Discrimination
abstract: Modulation of the frequency/phase of return radar signals, termed micro-Doppler analysis, has been extensively used to detect and classify various objects, e.g., drones and helicopters. In this contribution, a variation of this approach based on periodic micro-fluctuations modulating the power of the main Doppler return, is investigated. In 2020, Defence Science and Technology Group (DSTG) carried out a series of field experiments to collect data on the radar returns from various drones. Micro-modulations of the phase and power of each UAV’s body Doppler return were analysed and compared. Series of harmonically related spectral lines, characteristic of each UAV, were observed, particularly in the power. Additionally, for the analysed data, the fundamental frequency of these harmonics was found to be correlated with the weight of the drone suggesting that the proposed approach may be useful in providing easily obtained features that can be used to augment other approaches to drone classification.

articleTitle: Data Segmentation and Fusion for Classification of Armed Personnel Using Micro-Doppler Signatures
abstract: In recent years, convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have been increasingly used for classifying radar micro-Doppler signatures of various targets. However, obtaining large amounts of data for efficient CNN training in defence and surveillance scenarios can be challenging. Therefore, designing techniques that maximize the use of available samples is critical. In this paper, we propose an approach built on the hypothesis that certain classes of radar spectrograms, such as those used for discerning armed from unarmed walking personnel, do not have information about the class encoded in the trajectory. Therefore, our method entails segmenting each input spectrogram into individual frames that correspond to a distinct step of human locomotion. Subsequently, we classify each segment independently and combine the resulting classification scores to obtain the final score for the entire spectrogram. As a result of this segmentation, the size of the training set is increased, whereas the dimensions of each sample—and therefore the number of parameters in the classifier—is decreased, reducing the risk of overfitting. Our experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach and its potential to enhance CNN-based classification of micro-Doppler signatures.

articleTitle: Interrupted Sampling Repeater Jamming Suppression Based on Time-frequency Segmentation Network and Target Signal Reconstruction
abstract: Interrupted sampling repeater jamming (ISRJ) with flexible modulation and fast response capabilities seriously damages radar detection performance. The effectiveness of existing methods declines significantly at low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) conditions. In this paper, an ISRJ suppression method based on a time-frequency segmentation network (TFSegNet) and target signal reconstruction is proposed. Utilizing the time-frequency (TF) separability of jamming and target signals, a TFSegNet is developed to automatically generate TF masks and extract the TF distribution of de-chirped target signals after jamming elimination. And the target signals reconstructed by inverse TF transform pass through a frequency-domain band pass filter to further eliminate noise. Simulation results verify the superiority of the proposed method in the low SNR and multi-target cases and the strong robustness to varying SNRs and jamming-to-signal ratios.

articleTitle: A Sub-array MIMO Radar Waveform Design with Wide Pulse Compression Main-lobe
abstract: Existing multiple-input multiple-output radar wave-form optimization works focus on full-digital radar, which is only a small part of existing radar system. Sub-array MIMO radar, in which sub-array antennas operate in the phased-array mode and different sub-array transmit differen waveforms, is more practical in some real applications. This paper studies a sub-array MIMO radar waveform optimization method. A waveform optimization criterion is presented to suppresses range compression sidelobes, mutual correlation sidelobes for differernt spatial regions, and the mismatch from a desired transmit beampattern. The sequential quadratic programming (SQP) algorithm is used to solve the optimization problem. Numerical results indicate that this method can efficiently control the distribution of signal energy in space and to suppress auto and mutual correlation sidelobes of angular waveforms.

articleTitle: Development of the Dust Ejecta Radar Technology (DERT) to Determine Plume-Surface Interaction Ejecta Velocities on Planetary Surfaces
abstract: Here we present a novel use of millimeter wave doppler radar to measure the velocity of ejecta generated by the impingement of rocket plumes on a planetary surface. The Dust Ejecta Radar Technology (DERT) provides a unique dataset based on direct measurements of ejecta particle velocities during plume-surface interactions. DERT is a continuous wave (CW) 94GHz radar unit that is being developed at Kennedy Space Center. DERT has measured velocities of a pendulum $(\sim 1 \mathrm{~m}/\mathrm{s})$, a rotating strip $(60 \mathrm{~m}/\mathrm{s})$, projected regolith simulant BP-1 $(\sim 250 \mathrm{~m}/\mathrm{s})$ and rifle rounds $(-820 \mathrm{~m}/\mathrm{s})$. Signal-to-Noise Ratios of up to 60 dB have been demonstrated. Data collected from DERT will inform the development of high-fidelity computational models of plume-surface interaction effects and will help address NASA Strategic Knowledge Gaps related to characterizing entry, descent and landing effects, and the risks associated with high-speed ejecta on the lander and lunar surface assets.

articleTitle: Low-Cost Vehicle In-Cabin Occupancy Detection Using An Approximate Model of XGBoost
abstract: This paper proposes a method of vehicle in-cabin occupancy detection using millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar and machine learning scheme. We develop a simple approximate model of extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) which improves explainability and simplicity of the method. XGBoost is a model composed of a huge number of decision trees, which can be approximated into a single decision tree unlike neural network (NN). The proposed simple model can easily be implemented on a low-cost firmware which is installed with radar modules. The performance of the proposed model is evaluated in comparison with NN and XGBoost-based model.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a Holographic Staring Radar for UAVs and birds Surveillance
abstract: The holographic staring radar is an array radar that looks everywhere all the time and performs multiple functions simultaneously instead of sequentially. It does not need to beam scanning and enables longer integration times and higher Doppler resolutions. This paper first provides a detailed introduction to the design of the holographic staring radar system, including the antenna, transmitter, receiver and signal processing module. Then, we conduct field trials with the developed radar in the airport and get the measured Doppler waterfall plots of five different targets. The extracted micro-Doppler features help to improve target recognition performance. As a consequence, the excellent performance in detecting, tracking and recognizing birds and UAVs is proved.

articleTitle: A Particle Swarm Optimization Approach to Surveillance Resource Management
abstract: Multi-function radar systems utilize electronically steered phased arrays and arbitrary waveform generation to perform tasks such as surveillance, tracking, and imaging on a single aperture. To take full advantage of these capabilities, new algorithms must be developed to efficiently distribute the finite time, energy, and processing budget of the radar between competing tasks. Much of the existing literature on resource management focuses on the tracking task, applying a fixed strategy for surveillance (e.g., a raster scan). This paper presents a novel representation of the surveillance environment that can be used to manage resources in phased array radar systems, using particle swarm optimization (PSO) to estimate the density of untracked targets in a search volume. The proposed algorithm, known as Surveillance PSO (SPSO), is computationally efficient for real-time operation, makes few assumptions about the environment or the underlying radar system, can easily be extended to simultaneous control of multiple beams, and provides an output representation that is a constant-length tensor that can be used directly as an input to a neural network. The efficacy of this approach is demonstrated by a series of simulated surveillance environments.

articleTitle: Lightweight CNN for HRRP Recognition Based on Attention Mechanism Structured Pruning
abstract: Deep convolutional neural network (CNN) has been widely investigated for radar target high resolution range profile (HRRP) recognition. However, the deep structures of CNN require high storage and computational capabilities, thus restricting its applications with limited resources. In this paper, we design a lightweight CNN model with structure pruning based on the channel-wise attention mechanism. Specifically, the attention value is used to represent the importance of the filters in CNN. Furthermore, Greedy strategy and fine-tuning are adopted in the pruning process to minimize the loss of model performance. The results of public dataset show that the recognition accuracy of the proposed method decreases by less than 0.13% when the pruning ratio is 80%.

articleTitle: Measurements of foliage attenuation using a drone
abstract: Foliage attenuation of radar signals is function of the length of the path travelled by the electromagnetic wave through the forest, i.e. the angle of elevation at which the signal propagates.An original concept is proposed to have a magnitude estimation of this absorption for P-band frequencies in function of elevation. The aim is to compare the level of signal received with antennas above and under the canopy from a source embarked on the drone flying above the forest.The results obtained and the characterization as a function of elevation show a good consistency with the values displayed in the literature.

articleTitle: Hybrid Approach for Reflective Surfaces Reconstruction Using Automotive Radar
abstract: Automotive radar is the main sensor enabling autonomous driving and advanced driver-assistance system (ADAS) capabilities. Its major role is to provide high-accuracy information on the vehicle surrounding. However, in dense urban environments, multiple objects limit radars’ line-of-sight and degrade their performance due to the multipath phenomenon, which generates ghost targets. Efficient radar’s operation in the presence of occluding and reflecting surfaces requires their accurate reconstruction. This work proposes a hybrid approach combining the model with the deep neural network to reconstruct the reflected surfaces from the received radar echoes. Accurate reconstruction of reflecting and occluding surfaces is expected to enable automotive radar non-line-of-sight operation and multipath-induced ghost targets mitigation. The ability of the proposed approach to reconstruct the reflective surface is evaluated via simulations, and its superiority over the conventional estimation approaches is demonstrated.

articleTitle: On the Recycling of Random FM Radar Waveforms
abstract: Random frequency modulated (RFM) waveforms have been found to possess a number of useful radar properties such as high dimensionality, good spectral containment, and amenability to high-power transmitters. Moreover, RFM waveforms can be optimized according to a desired spectral template and/or to obtain relatively low range sidelobes. Here we examine a way to greatly reduce the need for the optimization/ storage of new waveforms by performing “recycling” of existing waveforms that have already been optimized. It is shown via hardware loopback capture that recycled versions can largely preserve characteristics of the original while still producing sufficiently distinct new waveforms.

articleTitle: Study of long integration time passive radar processing techniques for low reflectivity drone detection
abstract: A study of different integration times used for different types of targets is proposed. Depending on the characteristics and movement of the target, the best integration time must be found. For targets with low reflectivity whose trajectory dynamics consist of high velocity and acceleration, it is important to find a compromise solution where the effects of range and Doppler spread do not decrese the detection capabilities. For high-reflectivity targets with slow trajectory motion, low integration times would be sufficient for detection. The study is based on the analysis of results obtained with real data acquired by a passive radar in a maritime scenario during Robotic Experimentation and Prototyping using Maritime Unmanned Systems (REPMUS) exercises.

articleTitle: The Effect of Transmitter Nonlinearity on Passive Radar Ambiguity Processing
abstract: Delay-Doppler processing in passive radar is enhanced by first preprocessing the reference signal to remove noise and impurities, usually by demodulation and reconstruction. However cancellation of the direct path component and stationary clutter returns can be impaired when a reconstructed reference signal is used. This study hypothesises transmitter nonlinearities as a potential cause of poor cancellation. The memory polynomial is chosen as a suitable model for transmitter nonlinearity (NL). Simulation studies demonstrate that neglecting to model nonlinearities on the reconstructed reference signal does not significantly affect ambiguity surfaces directly, but that peak-to-floor metrics are degraded when zero-Doppler cancellation is performed without nonlinear modelling. Analysis of single-channel real data yields a small improvement when nonlinearities are modelled.

articleTitle: Mirror Scanners for Panoramic Millimetre Wave Radars
abstract: To ensure that a vehicle mounted panoramic radar continues to illuminate the ground even in the case of base motion (roll and pitch) it is necessary to broaden the elevation beamwidth to generate a fan beam and maintain a reasonable swath width. This paper examines methods to achieve this for a 94 GHz swash plate scanner. Because of their rotational symmetry, swash plate scanners with flat mirrors produce pencil beams so some mechanism to widen the beam in elevation is required. This paper examines various methods to achieve this and concludes that shaping the mirror is the best option. A simple PCAAD-6 model was developed to predict this elevation beam spread based on the mirror curvature. Measurements were then made using both smoothly curved and stepped zone-plate mirrors that confirm the good accuracy of the predictions.

articleTitle: Ground-based Surveillance and Classification Radar for Wildlife Protection
abstract: Wildlife poaching has become an increasingly large problem over the last decade in southern Africa. There have consequently been worrying declines in rhinoceros population levels. As part of a multi-year effort to investigate and develop technology to aid in the prevention of poaching activities, a C-band phased array radar, with integrated ground target classification capability, has been produced. In a field trial that took place in the Kruger National Park Game Reserve in South Africa, it successfully detected and classified human and animal movement at ranges of up to 10 km. The misclassification rate of humans was less than 7%, and non-human movement, predominantly from animals and vehicles, was incorrectly classified as human 3.8% of the time. This shows that modern radar, without assistance from other sensors, has great potential to contribute towards the preservation of scarce wildlife resources.

articleTitle: Differential Phase Correction of Dual-polarization Weather Radar with Slotted Waveguide Antenna
abstract: The dual-polarization phased array weather radar (DPPAWR) uses a slotted waveguide antenna with high gain and low sidelobe radiation characteristics. However, the waveguide structure, slot position, and processing errors cause distance differences in the echoes of the horizontally (H) polarized channel and the vertically (V) polarized channel, which can lead to errors in the measured differential phase. Moreover, this error varies with the DPPAWR’s electronical scanning angle. Based on the slow change of the differential phase in the small precipitation area, this paper estimates and corrects the differential phase error using close-range weak precipitation echoes. The dependence of the differential phase error on the elevation angle (electronic scanning in elevation) is clarified, and a segmented formula for the initial differential phase and the elevation angle is obtained by quadratic polynomial fitting, which can correct the differential phase at close range and small precipitation area to 0. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified using precipitation data of different reflectivity observed on another day.

articleTitle: Multi-Static and Multi-Temporal ISAR Imaging of Non-Cooperative Air Targets
abstract: This paper introduces an approach for imaging non-cooperative air targets using multi-temporal and multi-bistatic ISAR techniques. The proposed method harnesses the power of multiple radar systems and longitudinal radar measurements to generate a high-resolution image of the observed target. The paper concisely overviews the practical theory underpinning bistatic ISAR imaging, emphasizing real-data results.

articleTitle: NovaSAR-1 Operational Updates and its Analysis Ready Data Production
abstract: Launched in September 2018, NovaSAR-1 is a technology demonstrator by Surrey Satellite Technology Ltd, UK (SSTL), and Airbus Defence and Space Ltd. The NovaSAR1 satellite utilises the only currently operational spaceborne S-band Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) providing medium and high-resolution images of Earth from space. Australia has secured a 10% capacity share in this mission, providing the nation with a first-ever sovereign civilian Earth observation satellite capability. The Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research organisation (CSIRO) operates this service as a National Facility for research, supporting science projects that are scoping the application of S-band SAR to terrestrial and marine environments. To make data from the mission accessible to non-expert users, CSIRO has developed NovaSAR-1 Analysis Ready Data (ARD) for the Normalised Radar Backscatter (NRB) product that is compliant with specifications set by the international Committee on Earth Observation Satellites (CEOS: CEOS-ARD NRB Product Family Specification v5.5). This paper provides CSIRO’s NovaSAR-1 operational updates, describes NovaSAR-1 ARD production with per-pixel metadata, and demonstrates early applications of NovaSAR-1 ARD products.

articleTitle: A portable many-element coherent receiver system for passive radar and space domain awareness
abstract: We describe a portable 32-antenna coherent passive radar system. The system was developed with space domain awareness in mind, but can be used for aircraft and nearer objects. We describe the physical and signal processing architecture and the results of a system test using VHF-band broadcast transmitters as illuminators. Using a combination of phased-array beamforming and delay/Doppler processing, the flight path of a small training aircraft was tracked with high accuracy in excellent agreement with public flightpath data.

articleTitle: Graph Data and GCN Based Maritime Target Detection of Multi-frame Scanning Radar
abstract: The research on sea target signal detection methods is valuable in many fields. Affected by the complex sea clutter environment and target features, it is difficult for conventional target detection methods to achieve high-performance detection. When deep learning methods such as convolutional neural networks are applied for radar signal processing, each signal sample is independent of each other, and the spatial-temporal relationship information cannot be effectively utilized. In recent years, Graph Convolutional Networks (GCN) have shown great advantages in graph data processing and have been applied in the field of signal processing. This paper proposes a maritime target detection method based on radar signal graph data and GCN, which converts radar multi-frame scanning signals into data with a graph structure, and uses GCN to perform binary classification on the nodes in the graph data to realize maritime target detection. Experimental results show that the proposed method has better performances that conventional 2D-CACFAR method with lower false alarm rate and higher detection probability.

articleTitle: Importance Differentiation Based Coordinated Anti-Jamming Strategy Optimization for Frequency Agile Radar
abstract: In modern electronic warfare, it is very important to develop smart multi-radar cooperative anti-jamming methods. However, the complexity of the environment and the limitation of radar resources make it very difficult to ensure the anti-jamming performance of all radars. Motivated by the problem, in this paper, a cooperative anti-jamming strategy optimization method based on importance difference is proposed in the scenario of multi-radar and multi-jammer antagonism. To describe the sequential radar anti-jamming decision-making process, a detailed Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (POMDP) model is formulated. Especially, we define importance factor to measure the importance level between radars. Based on the importance factor, the unique reward function is designed to be the weighted sum of the smart radar’s anti-jamming performance and other radars’ performance. Smart radar can guide other radars to achieve the purpose of cooperating anti-jamming or deceiving jammers. Simulation results show the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Signal Fusion-based Distributed Detection in Heterogeneous Radar Scenarios
abstract: In distributed radar system, local radar may form heterogeneous statistics which probability density functions (PDFs) are different, but it is typically difficult to combine such observations for better detection performance. In this paper, taking fusion of the cell-average constant false alarm rate detector and the square-law detector for instance, we propose a signal-fusion based distributed detection algorithm and its global test statistic is a sum of linearly weighted local statistics, which the local weights depend on the channel SNRs. According to the Neyman-Pearson criterion and under the assumption of independence of local observations, the optimal test statistic is a sum of complicated functions of local test statistics and thus its PDFs are difficult to obtain. We first find the equivalent local test statistics to ensure that the PDF of a sum of the equivalent local test statistics under the null hypothesis has a closed-form expression. Then we approximate the global test statistic by the first-order Taylor series of the local likelihood ratio functions and local test statistics are properly weighted. Numerical results show that the detection performance of the proposed method outperforms the decision fusion algorithm. It is also found that the proposed algorithm is robust to SNR estimation errors.

articleTitle: Intelligent Suppression of Interferences Based on Retroactive-DQN
abstract: This paper aims to investigate intelligent interference suppression strategies through reinforcement learning. Particularly, the Retroactive-Deep Q Network (R-DQN) is devised as the principle of updating suppression strategies by introducing a backtracking Q value, which links the evaluations in each step of training. At the analysis stage, three interferences, including the Interrupted Sampling Repeater Jamming (ISRJ), the SMeared SPectrugram (SMSP) jamming and repeater jamming, and five suppression methods are considered. Moreover, the selection probabilities of the implementation sequence for interference suppression between the R-DQN and the conventional DQN are compared. Numerical results corroborate the effectiveness and robustness of the considered suppression strategies.

articleTitle: Colocated MIMO Radar Anti-sorting Waveform Design based on Communication Camouflage
abstract: It is important to reduce the probability of radar transmit waveforms being sorted and identified by hostile Electronic Counter Measurement (ECM) devices. In practice, once the directions of ECM devices are located, camouflaging radar waveforms at corresponding directions as communication signals may obstruct these devices sorting signal. Colocated Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) radars can achieve desired performance through waveform optimization. In this paper, we use an optimized colocated MIMO radar waveform as a carrier, and force the synthesized waveforms in space to have communication signal characteristics by applying phase perturbation. The objective function is set to minimize the phase perturbation to maintain the original waveform performance basically unchanged, and a series of optimization criteria are proposed to camouflage communication signals in different situations. Taking optimization time into consideration, we transform these criteria into quadratic programming problems, which enables our proposed method to be performed online. At the end of this paper, we verify the effectiveness of the method through some numerical results.

articleTitle: Experiments on an ISAR-Communication System Using Continuous Phase Modulation and Mismatched Filtering
abstract: Due to the congestion of the electromagnetic spectrum, the need for spectral allocation has been tremendous in recent times. Should they have the ability to share their bandwidth, radar and communications systems could collaborate in order to alleviate the frequency spectrum. A possible way to create a joint radar-communication system is the use of communication codes to simultaneously transmit information and perform radar missions. In this paper, continuous phase frequency-shift keying codes are transmitted in an ISAR framework with the objective of creating radar images. Using such codes requires sidelobe mitigation, which is achieved via mismatched filtering. A civil aircraft is illuminated and imaged, and a comparison between the communication codes and the classical chirp case is provided. The communication code shows a more uniform sidelobe level than the chirp case, and they have the flexibility of performing communication tasks by transmitting information.

articleTitle: Fast classification of drones and birds with an LSTM network applied to 1D phase data
abstract: This study investigates a new type of drone classifier based on Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks. As a real-time surveillance system, the classification time of a drone detection radar is crucial. The motivation for this work is to develop a classification framework which has low latency in terms of data processing for the algorithm input. Theoretical modeling of a rotary wing drone and a bird wing flapping returns were done first to exhibit the difference in the patterns of the respective phase progressions. Then, 94 GHz experimental trial data containing 4800 sequences of drones, birds, noise and clutter were used to create a diverse training dataset of 1D phase data for supervised learning. A stacked LSTM network with tuned hyperparameters was generated to reduce the possible overfitting from a simple LSTM model. Validation accuracy of 98.1% was achieved for 2-class classification of drone and non-drone. Further performance assessment was then done with 30 unseen test data, where the network was able to correctly classify all the sequences. It is ascertained that this method can be ~10 times faster than a spectrogram based classification model, which requires additional Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) operations.

articleTitle: Dual-Mode FMCW Harmonic Radar Supporting Auxiliary Transmitter Operation
abstract: In this paper, we propose a dual-mode FMCW harmonic radar capable of both harmonic and intermodulation operation. The presented system prototype operates in the X band in the uplink (radar to the target) and the K-band in the downlink (target to the radar). For intermodulation operation, an additional external X-band tone transmitter is utilized to boost the target response. The viability of the proposed system is demonstrated in field tests using a passive harmonic tag as a nonlinear target.

articleTitle: Super-resolution Imaging Method for Swarm Targets Based on Group Lasso
abstract: Drone swarms are increasingly prevalent in military and civilian use scenarios, thus their effective detection and resolution are highly desirable. Traditional super-resolution imaging methods rarely utilize the prior information of the swarm distribution, thus the structural information of the target is prone to loss. Also, they cannot simultaneously meet the requirements of high resolution, adaptation to different signal-to-noise ratios (SNR), etc. In this paper, we propose a super-resolution imaging method based on the clustering and individual sparsity properties of swarm targets. We introduce group Lasso, a mixed $l_{1}$/$l_{f}$ regularization method to preserve the swarm structure and contour. Firstly, group Lasso is used as a regularization constraint to establishing the objective function and the alternating direction method of multipliers is used to solve the optimization problem. Then the swarm contours and quantities are obtained by constant false alarm detection, clustering, and convex hull algorithms in turn. Finally, simulation results are given under different swarm shapes and SNRs to verify the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Compensational Clutter Mitigation for Periodic Modified BFSK Waveforms in HF OTHR
abstract: The use of FSK-coded waveforms has been previously shown to potentially allow for target detection when the target Doppler is ambiguously aligned to a Doppler offset that is a multiple of the waveform repetition frequency (WRF) and therefore obscured by clutter sidelobes. This has been demonstrated, for example, with pseudo-random coded BFSK waveforms with the thumbtack ambiguity function. Detecting Doppler-ambiguous targets is of particular importance in HF over-the-horizon radar (OTHR), where blind zones due to clutter and/or clutter sidelobe masking is frequently encountered in the detection of high-speed targets. The need to suppress the ambiguous clutter sidelobes is of particular importance in applications with these waveform classes. The considered mismatched processing has been proven in earlier works to have two strictly equivalent realizations, as the optimum mismatched filter and also as compensational processing (the CLEAN technique) with optimum a posteriori clutter estimation. While the computational demands associated with forming these filters can be significant, it is shown here that filters can be largely pre-computed, allowing for real-time applications. We examine target processing losses associated with various perturbations of this clutter filtering technique.

articleTitle: Binary Quadratic Programming based Detector for Radar Target in Compound Gaussian Clutter
abstract: This paper considers the problem of radar target detection in compound Gaussian clutter background. Different from the existing detector design criteria, we firstly study the detection problem by introducing an auxiliary variable, as a consequence, the detection problem is recast into a binary quadratic programming (BQP) problem. Considering the binary nature of the auxiliary variable, we apply the relaxation algorithm to solve the BQP problem and propose a new detection scheme for the detection problem. Finally, simulation experiments are performed to verify the effectiveness of the proposed detector in comparison with several state-of-the-art detectors.

articleTitle: A time-frequency analysis method with joint speed estimation and translation compensation based on Near-Field MIMO Array
abstract: Micro Doppler analysis of human kinematics is widely used in the detection and recognition of human contraband. However, during the observation time (CPI), the translational motion of the human body introduces errors in the Doppler curve of the micro moving parts of body, thereby altering the Doppler dynamic range and causing folding and deviation of the micro Doppler curve. At this point, conducting time-frequency analysis directly on the echo data will result in significant errors. This paper proposes a joint algorithm of translational speed estimation and time-frequency analysis based on the MIMO near-field model. This algorithm not only achieves the estimation of translational speed, but also compensates for the phase error in the micro motion part of body, thereby improving the recognition performance of time-frequency maps. The effectiveness and superiority of this algorithm have been verified through simulation.

articleTitle: Maritime 3D-ISAR with Clutter Suppression
abstract: Three dimensional (3D)-ISAR has been developed to improve the target representation and provide more accurate estimates of a target’s geometric features. For example, after the dominant scatterers are extracted from the ISAR imagery, the length, width and height can be determined and used for classification. Unfortunately, if there is significant sea clutter in the scene, the scatterer extraction process will be confused by both the sea clutter and target returns. In this paper, we use both simulated and real data to demonstrate an efficient dictionary learning technique that suppresses the sea clutter prior to image formation and improves the robustness of the imaging process.

articleTitle: Parameter Tuning for Maritime Track-Before-Detect
abstract: Track-before-detect (TBD) is a joint detection and tracking approach that takes advantage of a targets motion over time. To work effectively, it requires latent parameters to describe the underlying dynamics of the targets relative to the sensor system. Determining the latent parameters is critical for success, with errors potentially resulting in failure of the tracking algorithm. In this paper, we propose a parameter tuning method for the Bayesian TBD algorithm known as the Bernoulli particle filter. The parameter estimation formulation uses a Bayesian framework with the particle Markov-chain Monte Carlo algorithm. Experimental results for a maritime radar scenario are used to validate the new algorithm.

articleTitle: Calibration and Estimation for FDA-MIMO Radar with Random Amplitude and Phase Errors
abstract: The combination of frequency diverse array (FDA) with range-angle-time dependent beampattern and waveform diversity in multiple input multiple output (MIMO) radar, namely, FDA-MIMO radar, offers additional degrees-of-freedom to enhance the overall system performance. The existing parameter estimation algorithms for FDA-MIMO radar are difficult to achieve effective target estimation when there is amplitude-phase error in the array antenna. In this paper, the proposed method can achieve the calibration and estimation for FDA-MIMO radar with random amplitude and phase errors. First, the signal model for FDA-MIMO radar signal model with random amplitude and phase errors is established. Second, the angle and range estimation is obtained by the spectral peak search method with reduced dimension. Then, the amplitude and phase error of each array element are estimated by the singular value decomposition and eigenvalue decomposition. Finally, the multiple simulation experiments show that in the presence of amplitude and phase errors, the existing algorithms have completely failed, but the proposed algorithm still has the ability to estimate the target with high precision.

articleTitle: Multi-polarization Features Fusion Detection of Marine Small Targets based on LSTM
abstract: This article introduces a novel detector based on long short-term memory (LSTM) networks which intelligently fuses multi-polarization features for detection of the marine small targets. Specifically, complex Doppler features of data with different polarization are designed to provide basis for differentiation of the target and the clutter. Then, LSTM cells are utilized to capture temporal dependencies of both amplitude and phase of the Doppler features, which have powerful sequence extraction capability. After that, the detector adaptively assigns the fusion weights into features of different polarizations to carry out weighted feature fusion. Finally, the detection results are given according to final binary classification results of clutter and target. Experiments on public IPIX database validate the effectiveness of the proposed fusion scheme and demonstrate that the proposed detector surpasses the detector that uses only single polarization features.

articleTitle: Gridless Bayesian Inference for DOA Estimation with Coprime Array
abstract: In this paper, we propose a gridless Bayesian inference based direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation algorithm with coprime array to overcome the basis mismatch arising in conventional on-grid sparse signal reconstruction based algorithms. Under Bayesian framework, the distributions of DOAs are assumed as mixtures of von Mises models yielding the continuous parameterization of the direction information, while the signals power is governed by a Bernoulli-Laplace model turning the sources number estimation into binary sequence detection. The Bayesian model is formulated on the second-order virtual coarray signals and the variational Bayesian inference is performed to realized accurate DOA estimation with increased number of degrees of freedom (DOFs). Simulation results show the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm especially at low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR).

articleTitle: Effect of SAR point spread function on the correlation of clutter
abstract: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) forms complex images of the ground and has a complex point spread function (PSF). In this paper, the effect of the complex PSF on the SAR clutter intensity image, as measured by the intensity autocorrelation function (ACF) and intensity spectrum, is determined. The SAR image intensity ACF is obtained in terms of the speckle intensity, the underlying cross-section, and the PSF intensity envelope using only convolution. This can then be used to derive the spectrum of SAR image intensity, which is equal to the spectrum of speckle intensity plus a couple of intuitively reasonable terms both divided by the K-distribution order parameter. Using the knowledge of how the clutter intensity spectrum changes under PSF disturbance allows the PSF characteristics to be determined. This could allow the spectral slope, p, of an ionospherically induced PSF to be measured from clutter. Measurement of ionospheric scintillation parameters from clutter will enable wide-scale ionospheric phenomena to be studies and improved autofocus algorithms.

articleTitle: Factors to Consider for Radiometric Calibration of Airborne FMCW SAR imagery
abstract: This study reports the work carried out to perform radiometric calibration of an airborne FMCW SAR test bed developed by the CSIR in South Africa [1]. Factors of the radar range equation are explored to study the multidimensional problem of radiometric calibration or radar. Emphasis is made on the effects of turbulent platform motion or airborne platforms on all of the Radar range equation variables.

articleTitle: Vector-sensing antenna for measuring the direction of arrival of ionospherically propagated HF radio signals
abstract: The ability to determine the direction of incident radio waves is useful in a wide variety of different applications. For high frequency (HF) radio waves, this is commonly done using wide aperture arrays of antennas. However, due to the long wavelengths of HF waves, such arrays must be physically large. A vector-sensing antenna system, using orthogonal triads of antennas to measure the electric and magnetic field components of the incoming waves, offers the possibility of making these measurements without requiring a large area or a large number of elements. In this paper we will look at the performance of various vector-sensing antenna configurations when used to receive HF radio signals, and explore some of the difficulties that may be encountered.

articleTitle: Ionospheric Variance Models: Impacts on Over-the-Horizon Radar Performance Prediction
abstract: Climatological models of the ionosphere, such as the International Reference Ionosphere (IRI), are often used to assess the performance of over the horizon radar (OTHR) over the wide range of climatological conditions in which they are expected to operate. To date these models have only considered the monthly median performance. In this paper we use a new climatological model of the ionosphere which includes the monthly ionospheric variance, to investigate the impact of ionospheric variability on the OTHR performance assessment models. We examine how this impact varies with the target RCS and OTHR system design parameters.

articleTitle: Latest Airborne Imaging System Development and Capacities in ONERA
abstract: After 40 years of research and development in Airborne Radar domain, that started with the well-known and historical high performances platform RAMSES, ONERA invested in the miniaturization and transfer of sensors to the SETHI (jet) BUSARD (motorglider) and SAR-Light (UAV) platforms and conduct many and various experiments in remote sensing.This paper presents these platforms and latest developments and results of associated sensors, and the ongoing and expected research and developments.

articleTitle: Automated ISAR Image Quality Assessment
abstract: Inverse Synthetic Aperture Radar (ISAR) is a widespread imaging technology used to characterise and classify non-cooperative targets. Unfortunately, the quality of ISAR imagery is highly variable due to the target dynamics that are constantly changing. This paper presents three automatic ISAR image assessment techniques that can be used to filter out poor quality imagery. They include convolutional neural network (CNN)-based regression, deep K-nearest neighbour (KNN) regression and traditional feature-based KNN regression. These techniques were developed to address the two key challenges in ISAR image assessment: noisy data sets and limited labelled data.
