To train techniques and quantify performance, 1000 simulated ISAR images were labelled by multiple operators and used for comparison against the automated techniques.

articleTitle: Passive Spacebourne SAR Using Opportunity of Illumination
abstract: Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) can operate regardless of the weather condition or the availability of sunlight. However, the cost of launching an active SAR satellite is still relatively expensive given the stringent requirements of high radio frequency (RF) power needed to illuminate the target. In this paper, we propose a framework for a passive SAR satellite that opportunistically captures signals transmitted by another nearby active SAR satellite. The idea of such opportunistic configuration is based on bistatic radar, where the passive radar is assumed to be capable of estimating the reference signal originating from the active satellite. The proposed geometry considers the passive satellite to be launched to follow the same orbital plane of the active one but with a small delay. In order to demonstrate the concept, a SAR simulator is utilized to generate the unfocused raw data, which is later on is focused using the range-Doppler (RDA) processing algorithm. According to the achieved results, the proposed technique is feasible to be applied and implemented practically on the future SAR systems to generate a low-cost and high-quality SAR image.

articleTitle: Analysis of coherent radar sea clutter with combined wind driven sea and swell
abstract: Radar systems operating in a maritime environment need to be able to detect targets against a background of sea clutter returns. Hence it is important to understand the statistical behaviour of these returns in order to optimise a radar system detection algorithm. In this paper low and medium grazing angle radar sea clutter are analysed, to separate the effects of wind driven sea and swell in the Doppler spectrum. The offset gamma distribution is an effective model for the Doppler centroid and width distributions, as well as the asymmetric profile of the spectrum itself. The mean Doppler velocity is mostly due to the wind driven sea, with a contribution from the orbital velocity of the swell. A revised model is proposed for the mean Doppler shift as a function of grazing and azimuth angles.

articleTitle: Over-The-Horizon Radar Frequency Management System using the Assimilation Canadian High Arctic Ionospheric Model (A-CHAIM)
abstract: A frequency management system (FMS) is a critical component of the over-the-horizon radar (OTHR). The FMS has two subsystems: the spectrum monitor and the environmental monitor. The results of the sub-systems are merged to extract available and feasible frequencies for OTHR operation. An accurate ionospheric model is a vital component of the environmental monitor. The environmental monitor uses the recently updated Assimilation Canadian High Arctic Ionospheric Model (A-CHAIM) with the quiet D-region and precipitation-enhanced E-region modules to the electron density profile, which at present is the most accurate model available for real-time use in high-latitude regions. A-CHAIM, incorporates near-real-time data into a background model to account for the rapid changes that often occur in the high-latitude and polar ionosphere. This demonstration between a simulated transmitter and four targets in northern Canada was performed during the day and night of November 17, 2021 (fall) and June 17, 2022 (summer). A-CHAIM is now being used for OTHR trials and is used in the real-time FMS.

Author Keywords: Assimilation Canadian High Arctic Ionospheric Model (A-CHAIM)

articleTitle: Introduction to cognitive micro-Doppler radar: Optimization and Experiment
abstract: In this paper, we introduce the concept of cognitive micro-Doppler radar and investigate the impact of adjusting the wavelength, pulse repetition frequency (PRF), and coherent processing interval (CPI) on the micro-Doppler signals of a DJI Phantom 4 drone and a P750 aircraft. We propose metrics to quantify the quality of micro-Doppler signals and provide equations to optimize these signals. Our results demonstrate that cognitive micro-Doppler radar is a viable approach, and that changes in CPI and PRF values have differential effects on Jet Engine Modulation (JEM) spectra and the "blade flash" patterned Doppler spectrograms. Considering that the concept of cognitive micro-Doppler radar is still in its infancy, further research is necessary to explore its full potential and design. In summary, this paper serves as an initial exploration of cognitive micro-Doppler radar, providing valuable insights for future investigations.

articleTitle: Joint Design of Transmit and Receive Beamforming for Active RIS-aided Array Radar
abstract: This paper introduces an active RIS to assist the array radar receiver for performance improvement. To achieve maximum output SINR, we jointly optimize the transmit beamformer, the receive beamformer and the amplitude-phase control matrix of the active RIS, where the transmit beamformer is phase-only for high transmit power. We formulate the proposed codesign problem as a nonconvex constrained optimization problem and solve it under the alternating minimization framework. We first derive the closed-form solution of receive beamformer directly, and then determine the phase-only transmit beamformer and the RIS amplitude-phase control matrix by the Riemannian gradient method and the concave-convex procedure scheme, respectively. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed active RIS-aided radar significantly improves the output SINR and has the ability of suppressing more number of interferences.

articleTitle: Two Dimensional Resolution Improvement for FMCW Synthetic Aperture Radar Using Multistatic Configuration
abstract: Frequency-modulated continuous wave (FMCW) synthetic aperture radars (SARs) mounted on lightweight platforms cannot have highly resolved range and azimuth resolutions owing to hardware limitations such as load and power consumption. To overcome this, we propose a two-dimensional resolution improvement method using cross-track and along-track interferometry for range resolution improvement (RRI) and azimuth resolution improvement (ARI), respectively. First, RRI is performed for the FMCW SAR by combining two deramped FMCW signals depending on the spectral shift caused by the cross-track interferometry (CTI) configuration. Subsequently, for ARI, the Doppler frequency spectra of the signals are combined considering the difference between the Doppler centroids. Thereafter, a SAR image with improved range and azimuth resolutions can be generated. The simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed RI method in terms of resolution values; particularly, the proposed method can find adjacent point scatterers, which do not appear in conventional SAR images because of poor resolution.

articleTitle: A RARE-MUSIC Algorithm for Near-Field Target Localization with COLD-FDA-MIMO Radar
abstract: A rank-reduced MUSIC algorithm for near-field target localization with a Co-centered Orthogonal Loop and Dipole Frequency Diverse Array Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (COLD-FDA-MIMO) radar is addressed in this paper. The formulated near-field target localization problem is handled by sub-optimal design method based on the RARE criterion. The resulting locators demand, the solution of a box-constrained optimization problem for which parameter separateness and iterative techniques are exploited. Besides, the performance of the RARE-MUSIC architectures, which can reduce the computational complexity greatly and also have the same performance compared to the 5D-MUSIC algorithm, is evaluated via Monte Carlo simulations and compared with the benchmarks in Cramér-Rao Bound.

articleTitle: Statistical Feature Vector (SFV) For SAR ATR
abstract: Historically, Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) Automatic Target Recognition (ATR) has faced challenges and performance issues because the tendency is to treat SAR imagery the same way we treat optical imagery, whereas SAR complex images are fundamentally a clutter map that only resembles an image. As indicated by the name itself, the Statistical Feature Vector (SFV) is a radar phenomenology-based ATR engine that can map many image processing enhancements to the radar domain, while also including radar unique capabilities that can improves SAR ATR. An SFV is based on information theoretic compression of the SAR target formed from a complex Wiener filter that exploits the holographic nature of SAR images. For example, the Multistage Wiener Filter (MWF) may be used that determines the most compressed scattering space (potentially statistical combinations of scattering center elements) that represent the target. The SFV is shown to be a type of sufficient statistic for SAR ATR where methods of employment are the subject of ongoing research.

articleTitle: MATLAB-based Multistatic Passive Radar Demonstrator
abstract: The paper presents a realization of a multistatic passive radar demonstrator using the MATLAB environment. The hardware infrastructure of the system is located in the city of Przasnysz, Poland, and it consists of four stations that are located in the vicinity of an airfield that was purchased by the Warsaw University of Technology. The processing realized by the demonstrator implemented in MATLAB works online at a rate close to real-time. This allows observation and verification of the system operation to be easily performed. At the same time, the fact that the algorithms are implemented in MATLAB enables easy and quick modifications of the system.

articleTitle: Potentials of multi-aspect and multi-frequency radar imaging illustrated by experimental results in Ka- and W-band
abstract: Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) images especially of man-made objects are very sensitive to variations in aspect angle and frequency. Even small changes to the viewing direction or the center frequency can have a great impact on the calculated reflectivity image. This additional information on targets could be used to improve the performance of target recognition and identification. This paper discusses and illustrates the potentials of multi-aspect and multi-frequency SAR using airborne SAR data from a NATO SET-250 campaign in the UK.

articleTitle: An Inverse Reinforcement Learning Method to Infer Reward Function of Intelligent Jammer
abstract: This paper takes into account a frequency-agile radar system designated as “us” and an adversarial spot jammer designated as “enemy”, where the enemy jammer is modeled as an agent, and the radar’s strategy is characterized by its state transition probability in a Markov decision process (MDP). To comprehend the underlying attack motives of an intelligent jammer, a radar system must infer the utility function of the jammer. To accomplish this, the radar system must gather a dataset of actions taken by the jammer through observation of their transmitted signal. Next, a maximum entropy inverse reinforcement learning approach is utilized to recover the jammer’s reward function. After recovering the jammer’s reward function, the radar can infer the jammer’s attack intent, and develop appropriate anti-jamming strategies to effectively mitigate against the intelligent jammer. Simulation results demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Multifunctional Radar and Data Link Functions for Dual Use Applications
abstract: The aim of this paper is to explore the potential for dual use application of radar and data link functions using the same frequency range on a common hardware, specifically an Active Electronically Scanned Array (AESA) antenna with multi-channel radar backend architecture. By utilizing software-defined solutions, both radar and data link functions can be applied to the AESA antenna. For the purposes of unidirectional data link test applications, a large, broadband AESA-based multifunctional radar was used. This approach has the potential to allow for significantly higher data rate transmissions compared to today’s typically separated data link and airborne radar hardware. This can be achieved due to larger apertures leading to highly focused antenna beams, higher RF output power, and typically higher bandwidths of airborne surveillance and fire control radars compared to separately used data links.Experimental results from a laboratory set-up in an anechoic chamber are presented to demonstrate the potential data transfer rates achievable through this shared AESA radar-data link architecture. During the data transmission phase in radar pulse operation, very high data rates were achieved in various transmission modes, with average data transmission rates of over 400 Mbps.

articleTitle: An Intelligent Jamming Strategy Design Method Against Frequency Agility Radar
abstract: Frequency agility (FA) radar can avoid jamming by changing its carrier frequency, which makes it difficult for conventional jammers to cope with. In this paper, an intelligent jamming strategy design method is proposed. The process of the jammer and the FA radar confrontation is modeled as a Markov Decision Process, in which the jammer and the FA radar act as the agent and environment, respectively. The reinforcement learning algorithm, Proximal Policy Optimization, is selected to solve the jamming strategy design problem. To overcome the problem that the jamming effect cannot be evaluated by jammers in time-sharing mode, a decision approach of periodic action-evaluation is proposed. To evaluate the performance of the jammer, we elaborately designed a reward function with three components: intercept reward, launch reward, and evaluation reward. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method can learn highly adaptive strategies in the FA radar countermeasure scenarios and achieve good jamming performance.

articleTitle: High Resolution Inverse Synthetic Aperture Radar Frequency Estimation using Fast Iterative Interpolated Beamformer
abstract: This paper investigates the application of Fast Iterative Interpolated Beamformer (FIIB) to achieve high resolution Inverse Synthetic Aperture Radar (ISAR) images. FIIB is a low complexity frequency estimator which offers high levels of accuracy, making it suitable for ISAR Doppler processing. This study conducts simulations to evaluate the effectiveness of different frequency estimation techniques. FIIB is shown to produce highly focused images and outperforms the baseline Fast-Fourier-Transform (FFT) and MUltiple SIgnal Classification (MUSIC) algorithms across several metrics.

articleTitle: Scene Characteristic Mining-Based Semisupervised Network for Ship Detection in SAR Images
abstract: Deep synthetic aperture radar (SAR) ship detection networks can achieve excellent performance by training with lots of target-level labels. However, obtaining target-level labels is extremely difficult in practice. In this paper, a scene characteristic mining-based semi-supervised network (SCMS-Net) is proposed for SAR ship detection to address this issue. This network can leverage scene-level labels of SAR images for enhanced performance when the target-level labels are limited. Our approach extends the fully supervised RefineDet network by incorporating a dedicated scene characteristic mining branch (SCMB). By effectively utilizing scene-level labels, SCMB can extract scene characteristics in SAR images that are beneficial for representing ships and clutter, thereby achieving higher performance. Additionally, a hierarchical test process is proposed in this paper. It can reduce false alarms in inland and inshore scenes, as well as missing ships in the offshore scene. Experiments based on an authoritative SAR ship detection dataset validate the effectiveness of our method.

articleTitle: Factors Affecting the Effective Clutter Rank for Planar and Conformal Antennas with Subarrays
abstract: The Effective Clutter Rank (ECR), the number of eigenvalues of the clutter covariance matrix larger than the white noise, has important consequences for the radar system when suppressing clutter with Space-Time Adaptive Processing (STAP), in terms of cost, complexity, usability and performance. In this paper some factors affecting the ECR are studied by simulations. The result is partly explained by theory from the literature. The main results are: 1) Factors affecting the ECR [subarray beam pointing direction, subarray design, antenna geometry, # radar pulses, PRF, radar velocity and target range]. 2) Differences between planar and conformal antennas. 3) A simulation-based rank calculation method for antennas with subarrays.

articleTitle: Urban Clutter Analysis for Drone Detection using L-band Staring Radar
abstract: Stationary ground clutter can present a significant challenge for radar detection of moving targets particularly for low altitude slow moving small targets such as drones. In urban environments, clutter returns from collections of man-made structures can cause obscuration and introduce multipath that can interfere with the echoes of the targets of interest. Furthermore, phase noise in the presence of strong stationary clutter can lead to masking weaker signals from slow moving objects such as small unmanned aircraft systems (sUAS). This work focused on the analysis of urban clutter in the Birmingham area using two L-band staring radars to provide detailed characterization of clutter of a dense urban environment. Clutter maps are generated at various Doppler frequencies to understand the impact on target signal-to-noise ratio as a result of strong ground clutter. This work will provide a basis for establishing radar sensitivity against low observable targets in built up areas.

articleTitle: Calibration of a Radar Cross-section Model using a Surrogate Model Optimization Algorithm
abstract: EMPRISE<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup> is a software package under development used by sensor and radar system companies, as well as the French government for its equipment programs. The software simulates the IQ signals received by a radar system from the digital twin of a radar scene. The goal of any simulation software, such as EMPRISE<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup>, is to quantify the performance of a given radar system in a given environment. To improve the software representativeness of these simulators, it is necessary to calibrate the radar material cross-sections used by the scene model according to measurement data. In this paper, we propose a calibration method, applied to EMPRISE<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup>, based on an adaptive surrogate model and a minimizing search algorithm.

articleTitle: Enhanced Target Tracking Based on Novel 5D Millimeter-wave Automotive MIMO Radar
abstract: With the rapid advancement of radio frequency (RF) and the integrated circuit (IC) technology, millimeter wave (mmWave) multi-input multi-output (MIMO) radar, as one of the mainstream sensors, is widely used in automotive industry. The conventional 4-dimensional (4D) mmWave MIMO automotive radar can only estimate four parameters, those are distance, radial velocity, azimuth and elevation, which may render the vehicles insensitive to the targets with small radial movement. For example, vulnerable road users (VRUs), who suddenly cross the road, exhibit almost zero radial velocity for the driving cars towards them. Transversal velocity, which is a complement of radial velocity, is required to accurately track the moving target. In this regards, this work proposes a novel 5D mmWave MIMO radar, which is able to track the moving target in higher accuracy by adding the fifth dimension of transversal velocity compared with the conventional 4D counterparts. Different from our previous work, where the interferometry was performed at the receiver, this paper estimates the transversal velocity via combining receive beamforming and transmit interferometry. Finally, we test the proposed 5D MIMO radar in experiments, and the results manifest the effectiveness of the proposed novel 5D mmWave MIMO radar in terms of trajectory tracking.

articleTitle: SAR Image Correction of Moving Ships in Marine Scene based on Wakes
abstract: For marine environments, it has been perceived in actual synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images that the radial velocity of a moving ship causes an azimuthal displacement and the azimuthal velocity smears SAR images. In order to eliminate these effects caused by the motion of moving targets in SAR images, the estimation of moving speed and direction is necessary. In former works, these parameters are mainly estimated based on SAR echoes with the technology of signal processing. However, in a marine environment, there exists ship wake waves which are generated by the ships and are related to the velocities of ships, so in this paper, the generated ship wakes are regarded as a tool to inverse the velocities and moving directions of ships. Then the SAR imaging algorithm with known velocities of the moving targets is applied to correct the SAR images. All of the numerical results show the good performance of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Impact of Transmitter Elevation Pattern on Multi-frequency DVB-T Passive Radar Detection of Airborne Targets
abstract: In this paper, some aspects of passive radar air surveillance are addressed. It is well known that multiple antennas and frequency channels increase detection capability and that transmitter antenna pattern plays an important role in target detection. In order to evaluate the capability in a practical scenario, a measurement campaign was conducted, in which two airborne targets flew in pre-determined trajectories, covering different flight headings, altitudes and distances from a DVBT DTV broadcasting station. The three most important factors with regard to SNR on both targets were identified as receiver and transmitter antenna pattern and receiver positioning. For the transmitter pattern, the pattern causes nulls at some angles. As these null positions are frequency dependent, a good choice of transmitter bands will minimize risk of lost target detection. This fact could clearly be observed in the measurement data. Another aspect studied was the antenna placement. The measurement campaign consisted of two days. The first day, the surveillance antennas were placed on the top of a hill, with LOS to transmitter and the next day hidden behind a small ridge on the hill, relative to the transmitter. There was a significant improvement in SNR just by placing the antennas protected from LOS.

articleTitle: Area Preserving Linear Transformations and Spread Doppler Clutter Mitigation in Over-the-Horizon Radar
abstract: The use of recurrent waveforms in over the horizon radar (OTHR) necessitates techniques for ambiguity resolution and manipulation. In this paper, we elucidate methods for systematically transforming any given waveform, so that its ambiguity function is transformed by any desired area preserving linear transformation of delay-Doppler plane. Furthermore, given the desired delay-Doppler transformation, the corresponding waveform transformation can be explicitly constructed through the factorisation of $2\times 2$ matrices. Using this theory it is shown that the usual phase and frequency coding techniques used for range folded spread Doppler clutter mitigation, which induce an approximate Doppler shearing of delay-Doppler plane, can be replaced by chirp modulating the recurrent waveform. These non-recurrent chirped waveforms induce an exact Doppler shearing and lead to simpler and more robust signal processing of the returns.

articleTitle: RADAR 2023 Cover Page
Angular dependence of RCS enhancement due to phase screens
abstract: When a wave propagates through a phase screen to impinge upon a target, and is then reflected back through the phase screen, it experiences an increase in mean power. This effect has recently been observed by space-based radar imaging the ground through a turbulent ionosphere, but is also observed with optical phase screens. In this paper, it is shown that the enhancement in the mean is equal to the covariance between the forward and backward propagating waves. The statistics of a gamma (or Nakagami-m) distributed one-way intensity are used to derive the probability density function (pdf) of the two-way intensity for any arbitrary correlation between the waves. It is shown that the covariance is the correlation divided by the order parameter. The one-way intensity power spectrum is then used to derive the correlation as a function of position. It is shown that the enhancement occurs over the Fresnel zone, and immediately outside this is a region of reduced mean power, thus conserving energy. The analytical form of the correlation shows good agreement with the intensity correlation measured experimentally by a GPS receiver. The analytical theory conserves energy for a diffusion type phase screen.

articleTitle: Doppler Characteristics of Sea Clutter at K-band and W-band: Results from the St Andrews and Coniston Water Trials
abstract: This study reports on the experimental results from two field trials conducted by the University of St Andrews, focusing exclusively here on Doppler data. The first trial was at the Bruce Embankment in St Andrews, UK (winter 2020) and the second one was at Coniston Water in the Lake District, UK (autumn 2022). A 24 GHz K-band radar and a 94 GHz W-band radar were used in both trials to collect sea clutter data for phenomenology studies. As very few sea clutter data and analysis of these are available in the literature at these high frequencies, the results are expected to be of general interest within this field of study. The data collection at both trials was done for low grazing angles in the littoral zone. The datasets are quite varied in terms of wave direction, polarization and wind speed. The Doppler signatures and corresponding statistical parameters for these various conditions are reported here. The spectral analysis of different wave types (burst, whitecap, rough surface scattering) along with the combined spectra are also discussed. It is anticipated that these empirical results will be the precursor for improving upon the frequency ranges of existing sea clutter Doppler models.

articleTitle: Introducing a Multichannel Active Radar System for Research and Collaboration
abstract: A key technology for enhancing the capabilities and performance of radio-frequency (RF) systems in radar, communications and electronic warfare (EW) applications is the Active Electronically Scanned Array (AESA). The practical demonstration of robust AESA techniques in operationally relevant environments is critical to providing the confidence required to invest in the transition of innovative research to next-generation AESA-based RF capabilities for military and civil end-users. The Australian Defence Science and Technology Group (DSTG) has developed an L-band Multichannel Active Radar System (MARS) as a concept technology demonstrator (CTD) for this purpose. This paper introduces the system design and nominal capabilities of the MARS facility. It also presents preliminary results of real-time adaptive processing for interference mitigation using standard techniques.

articleTitle: DNN-based Beamforming for Mainlobe Interference Mitigation
abstract: This paper focuses on the design of a novel data-dependent beamforming algorithm based on Deep Neutral Network (DNN) for mainlobe interference mitigation. At the design stage, a DNN with four hidden layers is adopted, where the Parametric Rectified Linear Unit (PReLU) is utilized as the active function, and the Adaptive Moment Estimation (Adam) is performed as the optimization algorithm. Particularly, the signal received in the phased array is utilized as the DNN input, and the DNN output is obtained via the ideal beampatern response. Therefore, the mainlobe interference is mitigated by creating a deep null within the mainlobe while preserving the shape of mainlobe. At the analysis stage, simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed DNN-based method in mainlobe interference mitigation and angle estimation accuracy of the target.

articleTitle: Error Function Analysis and Simulation of Radar Range Discriminator for the RGPO/I Range Deception
abstract: The range deception against the range tracker is used in electronic warfare (EW). The radar range discriminator (RRD) error originates while tracking a target with a radar. RRD error is minimized while tracking the target. Hence, the range deception requires the presence of RRD error. Unidirectional range deception (URD) that increases or decreases the distance between radar and target can be used to introduce RRD errors. EW technique can be defeated by the electronic counter-counter measurements (ECCM) capabilities of a radar. A recent study proposed bi-directional range deception (BRD) with different velocities in opposite directions to overcome ECCM. However, the limited simulation was performed without the radar automatic gain control (AGC) in the low-jamming-to-signal ratio. This study analyzed the RRD error function due to the radar AGC by the BRD with acceleration and velocity based on the jamming-to-signal (JSR). The result showed that the values of the error function of RRD differed depending on overlap, separation, and gate departure within the early-late gate. Simulation and analysis results agreed at JSR=20dB.

articleTitle: Reconstruction of Fine Cross-Range Resolution ISAR Images of Targets in 3-D Motion using Compressed Sensing and Frame Selection
abstract: The Inverse Synthetic Aperture Radar (ISAR) is a powerful tool for target recognition and classification. However, generating focused ISAR images of moving targets is challenging because of motion compensation problems. In this study, we propose a novel approach to reconstruct an ISAR image of a noncooperative maneuvering target with 3-D motion using compressed sensing with a frame selection scheme. The proposed approach finds the time frames with only 2-D motion through a joint time-frequency analysis (JTFA) and Radon transform and reconstructs the ISAR image with an improved cross-range resolution by adopting compressed sensing. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in improving the image quality and reducing the impact of 3-D motion on ISAR imaging.

articleTitle: A Reduced-Dimensional STAP Scheme for End-Fire Array Airborne Radar
abstract: Compared with traditional broadside array, end-fire array has the advantages of low profile and strong directional radiation thereby is well-suited for airborne platform to detect moving target. Similar to the airborne radar with broadside array, the end-fire array airborne radar (EFAAR) also face the challenge of suppressing strong ground/sea clutter in practical application. However, the existing researches on clutter suppression for EFAAR primarily focus on the column-Doppler domain, while neglecting the clutter three-dimensional (3D) coupling characteristic. In this paper, a space-time 3D clutter signal model for EFAAR that incorporates the row spatial frequency, column spatial frequency and Doppler frequency is firstly constructed. Then, the clutter coupling characteristics in the row-column-Doppler 3D domain are analyzed in detail. Finally, a novel clutter suppression scheme for three typical scenarios is proposed according to the clutter distribution. Simulation results validate the superiority of the proposed scheme in both clutter suppression performance and training sample requirements.

articleTitle: Bayesian Filtering and Smoothing with Unknown Measurement Noise Covariance
abstract: Bayesian filtering and smoothing problems with unknown measurement noise covariance are investigated for linear Gaussian systems. The measurement noise covariance is assumed to be inverse Wishart distributed. A Bayesian filter and smoother calculating the joint posteriors for the state and the measurement noise covariance are derived by using a scale Gaussian approximation of t-distribution and moment matching. The proposed filter and smoother are non-iterative unlike the existing Bayesian solutions in the literature. The performance of the proposed algorithms is illustrated on a two-dimensional target tracking scenario. The simulation results show that the proposed filter and smoother have similar performance as the state of the art solutions with lower computational load.

articleTitle: Mitigating Range-Ambiguous Clutter Impact in Pseudo-Aperiodic Waveforms Using Adaptive Processing
abstract: Phase diverse and waveform repetition interval (WRI)/pulse repetition interval (PRI) diverse radar waveforms provide a number of advantages including being robust to intentional interference sources. Techniques for processing such waveforms have been proposed previously but with some drawbacks. Some of these techniques require joint range-Doppler adaptive filters for the full waveform which is computationally complex for typical over-the-horizon-radar waveforms. Other proposed techniques degrade in the presence of range-ambiguous clutter. In this paper, we introduce an adaptive processing technique for mitigating the impact of range-ambiguous clutter in phase diverse and WRI/PRI diverse waveforms. The processing is separable in range and Doppler, thus computationally quite efficient. The technique is capable of suppressing strong ambiguous clutter returns.

articleTitle: Combining Radar Acoustic Sounding and Schlieren Imaging to Quantify Close-in Air Turbulence
abstract: This paper presents a novel sensor for the detection and characterization of regions of air turbulence that would be of use to improve UAV stability in bad weather. It consists of a combined Schlieren imager and a Radar Acoustic Sounding System (RASS) to produce dual modality “images” of air movement within the measurement volume. The ultrasound modulated Schlieren imager consists of a strobed point light source, parabolic mirror, light-block and camera to provide a fine scale projection of the acoustic pulse modulated air turbulence through the measurement volume. The narrow beam 40 kHz/ 17 GHz RASS produces spectra based on Bragg enhanced Doppler radar reflections from the acoustic pulse as it travels. Tests using artificially generated air vortices showed some disruption of the Schlieren image and of the RASS spectrogram. This should allow the higher resolution Schlieren images to identify the turbulence mechanisms that are disrupting the RASS spectra. As the Schlieren imaging modality is not amenable to operation from a UAV, the objective of the research is to use it to inform the output of the RASS to allow its stand-alone operation from an aerial vehicle.

articleTitle: Parameter Estimation of Rotary Drones in Far Distance using Long-Time Spectral Processing
abstract: We investigate the micro-Doppler effect generated by drone rotors in this work, with the aim of estimating relevant parameters and motion information of rotors from the received signal. The commonly used method, short time Fourier transform (STFT), may fail due to the deficiency of the signal accumulation gain, especially when the drone is far away from the observing radar. To counteract this issue, we focus on the rotor parameter estimation of drones in far distance using Long-Time Spectral Processing (LTSP). Although LTSP is capable of preserving a large processing gain, it cannot present instantaneous spectral information of rotors. Instead, a series of harmonics is produced by LTSP. Different from existing works, we provide a theoretical analysis on the LTSP, which explained the generation principle of harmonics with the rotational frequency as the fundamental frequency. Furthermore, we point out the limitation of cepstrum to distinguish frequencies of a multi-rotor drone and propose a multi-harmonic separation method using peak frequency sub-traction to break through the limitation. Both simulations and experiments have been conducted to validate the effectiveness of the theoretical analysis and proposed methods.

articleTitle: Fusion Model Using a Neural Network and MLE for a Single Snapshot DOA Estimation with Imperfection Mitigation
abstract: In this paper, we discuss the fusion of deep neural networks with the Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE) algorithm for estimating both the Direction Of Arrival (DOA) of MIMO radars and the number of sources for a single-snapshot scenario using a Minimum Redundancy antenna Array (MRA) with imperfections and evaluating it with synthetic and real-world data. The combination of Deep Learning (DL) with the classical MLE seems to be a viable solution for this problem, as it is less computationally intensive than a classical MLE while not losing generalization and being better at estimating the number of sources. In both our experiments, using synthetic and real-world data, our method performs close to MLE and appears to be a deployable solution for real scenarios. Besides reducing the computational load of MLE, the novelty of our model lies in the fact that the deep learning model learns the gain and phase errors as a function of the direction of arrival instead of applying a simple calibration.

articleTitle: Discrimination of Automotive Radar Distributed Targets
abstract: Automotive radars are the main sensor enabling autonomous driving and active safety, and therefore, are required to provide high resolution in dense urban environments characterized by multiple distributed and close objects. Real targets are usually distributed over multiple ranges, Doppler frequencies, and angular bins. Super-resolution techniques allow distinguishing adjacent point targets, but they are not able to handle distributed targets. This work proposes a computationally attractive approach for discrimination between closely distributed objects in practical urban scenarios. Each distributed radar target is represented as a set of multiple scattering points with the associated joint probability density function, defined considering their position, shape, and velocity. The distributed targets are detected and enumerated according to the maximum likelihood and the Akaike information criterion. The ability of the proposed approach to accurately discriminate close distributed targets is evaluated via simulations.

articleTitle: Distributed Radar Target Detection with Ordered Local Statistics*
abstract: In distributed radar with local radar sites using cell-average constant false alarm rate (CA-CFAR) algorithm, the signal fusion based detection algorithm has been studied. However, the order statistic (OS) CFAR algorithm, as another important detection algorithm, has not been considered in distributed detection with signal fusion. This paper presents two algorithms for distributed detection with OS-CFAR test statistics. The first algorithm is that it randomly selects multiple values of order statistics to estimate the noise power through the maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) criterion. The second algorithm selects one of order statistics to estimate the noise power, and the optimum detection statistic for the fusion center is developed based on the Neyman-Pearson criterion. In numerical results, an iterative method is used to estimate the decision thresholds and the location of the selected value in order statistic has been verified to have a significant impact on detection performance. In particular, performance of the optimum detection statistic in distributed OS-CFAR is superior to suboptimum statistic and nonparametric statistic when choosing value at the front of the order statistics, while the conclusion is opposite when choosing value at the end of the order statistics.

articleTitle: A Compound Jamming Signals Recognition Method Based on One-Dimensional Multi-Label Convolutional Neural Network
abstract: With the continuous development of interference technology, and interference equipment constantly updated, the future of the electromagnetic interference environment presents a wide attack spectrum, interference style, a combination of many forms, the use of variable strategies, spatial and temporal changes, and other characteristics, the interference environment faced by the radar from a single jamming signal environment changes to a compound jamming signals environment. Therefore, it is important to accurately identify the jamming components and combination styles of compound jamming signals. In this paper, a compound jamming signals recognition method based on a one-dimensional multi-label convolutional neural network (ID-MLCNN) is proposed. The method uses a two-way convolutional neural network to extract the features of the real and imaginary parts of the compound jamming signals data and uses a multi-class threshold optimization method to optimize the multi-label recognition results. The method is applied to the compound jamming signals recognition experiments, and the experimental results show that the method can effectively identify the jamming components and combination styles of the compound jamming signals.

articleTitle: First Results of DVB-S Based Passive Polarimetric Measurements of micro-Doppler Signatures of a Helicopter
abstract: The utilization of space-based transmitters as Illuminators of opportunity (IoO) offers many desirable characteristics for passive radar applications: wider, continuous and all-weather coverage including remote and offshore areas, higher reliability against natural disasters or physical attacks, and less sensitivity to multipath effects than terrestrial-based transmitters. DVB-S (Digital Video Broadcasting-Satellite) represents a widely used transmission standard enabling satellite-delivered broadcasting for digital television and radio services from geostationary orbits. As IoO for passive radar applications it offers comparably high bandwidths and provides dual polarized transmissions, which opens new possibilities in polarimetric passive radar applications. This paper describes the results of the deployment of such a radar for the close range surveillance of ground and air-traffic on the Frankfurt International airport.

articleTitle: Robust Detection in Distributed MIMO Radar
abstract: We consider the case where there are outliers in the observations and evaluate two robust detectors, namely the Clipped Log-Likelihood Ratio Detector inspired by Huber’s ratio test, and a $\alpha$–Trimmed Sum Detector. The detector’s robustness and performance in the presence of outliers are analyzed. We show these detectors provide reasonably good performance despite the presence of outliers in the observations. We also analyze the detectors breakdown points where the detectors can not yield any meaningful results.

articleTitle: Robust Adaptive Beamforming Based on MR-FDA-MIMO radar Jamming Suppression
abstract: In this work, an adaptive beamforming algorithm based on a minimum redundancy frequency diverse array multiple-input multiple-output (MR-FDA-MIMO) radar is proposed. The algorithm utilizes the transmit virtual domain signal of a MR-FDA-MIMO radar to perform transmit adaptive beamforming, overcoming the limitations of transmit array elements and suppressing multiple mainlobe deceptive jamming. To mitigate the beamforming performance degradation resulting from including the true target in the samples, the jamming plus noise covariance matrix is restructured to obtain the optimal performance of jamming suppression. To fully utilize the virtual degree of freedom (DOF) in the transmit dimension of MR-FDA-MIMO radar, sidelobe barrage jamming and mainlobe deceptive jamming are suppressed separately. Sidelobe barrage jamming is suppressed in the receive dimension. Multiple false targets are suppressed in the equivalent transmit dimension. The simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the algorithm.

Author Keywords: minimum redundancy frequency diverse array multiple-input multiple-output (MR-FDA-MIMO) radar

articleTitle: Multiple Mainlobe Jamming Suppression via Eigen-Projection Processing Blind Source Separation Algorithm
abstract: In this paper, a multiple mainlobe jamming suppression method is proposed based on eigen-projection processing and blind source separation. Initially, the proposed method suppresses the mainlobe jamming nearest to the target in azimuth by employing eigen-projection processing. Subsequently, the method utilizes blind source separation to separate the mixed signal, thereby extracting the target signal while suppressing the remaining mainlobe jamming. The proposed method addresses the problem of declining suppression performance observed in traditional jamming suppression methods based on blind source separation, especially when the jamming is located in close proximity to the target direction. The numerical results demonstrate that the proposed procedure is capable of suppressing multiple jamming signals and achieving excellent performance.

articleTitle: Group Counting Using Micro-Doppler Signatures From a 77GHz FMCW Radar
abstract: People counting and detection technologies have shown great versatility in various scenarios and have become an important tool for event organizers and city planners to optimize their operations. This paper presents a novel approach for people counting using Micro-Doppler Signatures (MDS) extracted from a Frequency-Modulated Continuous-Wave (FMCW) radar operating at 77GHz. The system utilizes the unique gait model of each individual, which results in a distinct instantaneous velocity over time, to generate the MDS that are later used to classify groups of different sizes with a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN). Those results are compared with using existing CNNs for image classification, in a transferred learning approach. The proposed system overcomes the limitations of existing camera-based people counting techniques such as the need for a clear line of sight and being affected by lighting conditions.

articleTitle: Ambiguity Removal from the Cassini Radar Rings Observations
abstract: This paper describes a set of Cassini radar data collected on Saturn’s rings in the last year of operations when the spacecraft was flown very close to the ring system. After describing the observing geometry, real aperture backscatter results are presented which reveal many of the interesting features of the ring system. There is potential for higher resolution results from these data, but first, the problem of range ambiguities present in the data needs to be handled. An algorithm for ambiguity removal based on solving a singular value decomposition is presented.

articleTitle: Multistatic dual-channel detection of drones: effects of PNT errors
abstract: A radar network solution to detect drones is presented that consists of low-cost low-size dual-channel moving receivers, which can be deployed on UASs and operate within the coverage of an existing cooperative or non-cooperative monostatic staring radar. The receivers exploit the use of a dual-channel design and therefore use a reference and a surveillance channel to operate coherently without the requirement of a shared synchronisation reference signal between the network nodes, which is one of the key limitations of other traditional multistatic radar network solutions. Drone detection and parameter estimation is achieved by fusing the information collected at the network receivers and rely on accurate Position, Navigation and Timing (PNT) information. In this paper, we investigate the effects of PNT errors on estimation performance for such a radar network.

articleTitle: First multi-channel results of the airborne SAR/GMTI sensor PAMIR-Ka
abstract: Fraunhofer FHR is developing a multi-channel airborne Ka-band sensor for synthetic aperture radar imaging and ground moving target indication operation, PAMIR-Ka. In a final state, the sensor will be equipped with active electronically scanned array antennas for a two-dimensional transmit (TX) and receive (RX) beam steering. At present, the sensor uses a standard gain horn TX antenna and four horn antennas to acquire the scene echos with parallel RX channels. The horn antennas are statically mounted for stripmap operation. In a measurement campaign at Aachen in Germany, the sensor acquired data of an urban ground scene including some moving objects with an RX antenna configuration that allows both dual-polarimetric and along track interferometric data analyses. The paper presents these first multi-channel results of PAMIR-Ka.

articleTitle: Target detection in mainlobe jammers with FDA-MIMO radar
abstract: In this paper, the target detection problem in the presence of mainlobe jammers is investigated in a frequency diverse array multiple-input multiple-output (FDA-MIMO) radar. Particularly, FDA-MIMO radar offers the special range degrees of freedom (DOFs) for the discrimination of the true target and mainobe jammers. At the formulation stage, the detection problem for the window under test (WUT) is formulated as a multi-hypothesis test, where the number, the positions, and the parameters of the signals (including true target and mainlobe jammers) are unknown. To tackle the formulated problem, we devise detectors in a sub-optimal way, i.e., penalized test, which incorporates the model order selection (MOS) criterion into the generalized likelihood ratio test (GLRT) criterion. At the analysis stage, simulation experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the designed detectors.

articleTitle: The Ingara Real-Time Demonstrator
abstract: The Ingara Real-Time Demonstrator (RTD) being developed at the Defence Science and Technology Group is seeking to upgrade the current Ingara sensor and processing capability to support the maturation of exploitation algorithms as well as acquire a wider range of target and clutter phenomenologies. A key focus will be on the real-time demonstration and base-lining of standard and new algorithms for target detection, tracking and resiliency in contested environments. This paper describes the RTD objectives, system architecture and current progress.

articleTitle: Enabling Intra-CPI Frequency Agility Via Backprojection Based Range-Doppler Processing
abstract: Increased congestion of the electromagnetic spectrum has led to an expanded interest in adaptive spectrum sharing techniques. To opportunistically utilize the spectrum, spectrum sensing techniques can be used to dynamically adapt to the spectrum on a pulse-to-pulse basis within a single coherent processing interval (CPI). Although intra-CPI pulse agility allows for more efficient use of the spectrum, it creates unique processing challenges. By transmitting pulses at different intermediate frequencies (IF) within a CPI, the pulses are no longer strictly coherent and, therefore, traditional range-Doppler processing techniques break down. This paper presents a signal model for frequency adaptive linear frequency modulated (LFM) waveforms and analyzes the impact on the slow time phase history. Additionally, a modified backprojection algorithm is presented that compensates for the distortion caused by the frequency hopping to produce a range-Doppler map with a focused target. In addition to the simulated analysis, this work will conclude with an experiment using frequency agile pulsed radar to measure a moving vehicle utilizing an USRP X310 software-defined radio (SDR) as a radar testbed.

articleTitle: Robust 3D Mobile Mapping with Radar Sensors: A Real-Time Approach for Autonomous Navigation
abstract: In this research paper, we present a novel approach for generating grid maps (elevation maps) from sparse 3D radar point clouds collected from a vehicle. Our approach considers the inherent geometric uncertainty of radar targets, represented by error ellipsoids. A real-time processing pipeline, which has the potential to support applications such as autonomous vehicles and robotics, is developed. Our method shows promising results in capturing rough terrain alterations in an outdoor setting. However, some limitations were observed, including challenges in capturing smaller structures, smooth surfaces, and the presence of artifacts in the generated maps. Future research will focus on addressing these limitations and further enhancing the performance of radar-based topographic mapping. A video, demonstrating the real-time radar-based mapping pipeline in comparison to a lidar-based mapping, is available at https://youtu.be/4Gbd8QKel3U.

articleTitle: X-band SAR Data Acquisition and Frame-based Imaging: Towards Wide Area Surveillance
abstract: This paper presents the X-band UAV-borne SAR data acquisition and imaging system developed at Prince Sultan Defense Studies and Research Center (PSDSARC) in collaboration with MetaSensing, Italy. The developed SAR system conforms with the SWaP constraints for our in-house developed UAV. A computationally efficient scheme is also developed for SAR image reconstruction, incorporating motion compensation and frame-based real-time focusing. A recent field trial for SAR data acquisition took place over the Perugia, Italy in December 2022. The developed frame-based SAR image focusing approach is evaluated using the collected data.

articleTitle: Classification of Marine Traffic Activities Using ES Sensors and A VAE-CapsNet Approach
abstract: We propose and analyse a new method for the classification of marine traffic activity via deep learning (DL) techniques using capsule neural networks (CapsNets) and variational autoencoders (VAEs). Passive electronic surveillance data is used from 24 hours of activity in Sydney Harbour, Australia, the data is gathered by the electronic support (ES) sensor and extracted to train the VAE-CapsNet model. To address the imbalance in the measured data, data sampling based on oversampling and under-sampling methods is used. According to experimental findings, the proposed system can cover the activity per hour and achieve several classes of 19 with the highest accuracy of 99.19% and less training time than the existing method.

articleTitle: Detecting Planes during Take-off in SAR images using GMTI methods
abstract: The detection of fast moving and accelerating targets in Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imagery is a difficult problem. SAR image formation assumes that all objects in the scene are static over the coherent processing interval. The challenge in detecting airborne targets is addressing large target acceleration and velocity values when observed over the comparatively long dwell times associated with SAR collection paradigms and waveforms (including PRF) designed for stationary scenes. These factors lead to excessive blurring due to uncompensated phase terms, significant range migration, and potential aliasing of target signatures. Furthermore the dispersion of the target signature can lead to poor target to clutter ratios (TCR), complicating their detection.This paper explores initial research into a hybrid Ground Moving Target Indicator (GMTI) detection method combining interferometric processing, acceleration compensation, autofocus, detection and tracking to detect a challenging Doppler unambiguous moving target, with the objective of continued detection and tracking of a plane during take off. A SAR signal model is presented that parameterises a moving target signature in terms of range and azimuthal target velocities and accelerations. Data driven approaches for estimating these motion parameters are examined and applied to experimental data acquired with the Ingara SAR sensor. The hybrid detection method was found to improve TCR by around 6dB, along with superior detection and tracking performance.

articleTitle: W-band Radar aboard of Unmanned Aerial System for Wire Strike Avoidance
abstract: Wire strikes pose a serious threat for small UAS flying below 120 m, as wires are difficult to detect with the onboard visual system. In this paper we experimentally tested the capability of a W-band miniaturized radar as wire strike avoidance system for a small UAS in autonomous operation. The radar successfully detected the wire and the UAS was able to change its trajectory according to the position of the wire retrieved by the radar, in all tests we performed.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Methods for 1 km Soil Moisture Retrieval from Sentinel-1: An Evaluation with Limited Training Samples
abstract: Spaceborne synthetic aperture radar (SAR) is a demonstrated technique for high resolution soil moisture mapping in Australia, with the machine learning methods being increasingly popular due to the coming big SAR data era. In this study, the performance of three commonly used machine learning methods, i.e., random forest (RF), artificial neural network, and support vector regression, were evaluated for soil moisture retrieval from Sentinel-l data using a small set of training samples. The evaluation was focused on the $O z N e t$ soil moisture network located in New South Wales, Australia, and the International Soil Moisture Network (ISMN) dataset. The results indicate that the RF model performed relatively well under the different datasets and can be considered a preferred choice for soil moisture retrieval. To achieve the target root mean square error (RMSE) of $0.06 \mathrm{~m}^{3} / \mathrm{m}^{3}$, 10% of samples should be used in the training phase of RF. All three methods performed worse in the off-site scenario and showed poor capability in spatial generalization.

articleTitle: Radio Frequency Interference Suppression by Adaptive Filter Design for High-Frequency Radar
abstract: High-frequency (HF) over-the-horizon (OTH) radar are often affected by radio frequency interference (RFI) from co-channel services. This paper proposes adaptive receive filter design to suppress the RFI via pulse compression. First, according to the Doppler characteristics of sea clutter and RFI, observation statistics are designed to detect the sea clutter region. Then, the RFI spectrum is detected using the consecutive mean excision (CME) algorithm based on the power spectrum analysis of residual sea clutter and noise. Finally, the receive filter is designed under an adaptive similarity constraint and then used for pulse compression. Simulation results show that the proposed scheme can detect and suppress RFI accurately.

articleTitle: A Cognitive Radar Anti-Jamming Strategy Generation Algorithm based on Dueling Double DQN
abstract: With the improvement of the cognitive ability of the jammer, the electromagnetic countermeasure environment has become more complex, posing significant challenges to the anti-jamming performance of cognitive radar. Cognitive radar’s anti-jamming capabilities often depends on the correct generation of anti-jamming strategies, which makes the strategy generation a research hotspot cognitive radar anti-jamming. This paper proposes a cognitive radar anti-jamming strategy generation algorithm based on Dueling Double DQN (D3QN). The algorithm utilizes the state-value function and advantage function to estimate the quality of each radar echo and signal, thereby reducing the update error of the policy network. Additionally, to improve the speed of strategy generation, the proposed algorithm directly inputs the original echo into the policy network. Simultaneously, a jammer model with different working modes and interference type is established, and the corresponding jamming strategy is generated by the received echo, which is closer to the real confrontation environment. The effectiveness and robustness of the proposed algorithm are verified through high-fidelity adversarial experiments with variable jamming strategies.

articleTitle: Element Space DOA Estimation for Directional Transmission Scanning Phased Array Radars
abstract: Apart from MIMO, high resolution techniques for phased array radars such as optimum beamforming and MUSIC ignore the transmit beam pattern and work solely with the receiver outputs. However for directional transmit phased arrays which scan a relatively narrow beam over a restricted sector of interest ignoring the transmit beam pattern leads to model mismatch. The consequent losses can be mitigated by stacking the receiver outputs as the transmit beam is scanned over the sector of interest and modifying the steering vectors for the subsequent processing. This proposed hybrid approach can be interpreted as a MIMO virtual array system achieving higher beam output SNRs whilst still providing the MIMO ability to resolve more DOAs than conventional phased arrays. Numerical and simulation examples are presented to illustrate the stacked approach and to compare the different approaches to estimating the DOAs of uncorrelated signals.

articleTitle: An FDA-MIMO-Based Range-Ambiguous Clutter Sensing Approach for STAP
abstract: Space-time adaptive processing (STAP) via dynamic clutter sensing can effectively suppress heterogeneous clutter, but the clutter suppression performance will be seriously degraded in scenarios with range ambiguities. To tackle this issue, this paper proposes a clutter sensing approach with airborne frequency diverse array (FDA) for multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar. The proposed approach first uses FDA-MIMO radar to transmit sensing signals, which exploits the degree of freedom (DOF) in the range dimension. Then, a complete dictionary matrix in the range-angle-doppler domain is constructed. Finally, sparse recovery technology is used to reconstruct radar cross sections of clutter patches from sensing echoes, this prior information can assist STAP obtain better clutter suppression performance. Compared with the existing clutter sensing methods, the proposed method introduces the DOF in the range domain into the dictionary matrix, which can effectively improve the sensing performance of radar on range-ambiguous clutter, and then improve the suppression performance of STAP on heterogeneous clutter in the case of range ambiguity. Numerical experiments confirm the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Real-Time Implementation of a DPCA GMTI Technique for a UAV SAR Demonstrator System Developed by the CSIR
abstract: This paper presents a real-time Displaced Phase Center Antenna (DPCA) Ground Moving Target Indication (GMTI) processor. The GMTI processor performs clutter suppression, target detection, target tracking and target geolocation in real-time on a C-band airborne UAV radar demonstrator system. The processor is implemented on the GPU to meet the real-time performance requirements. A clutter suppression extent of 12.1 dB is achieved per frame in real-time.

articleTitle: Unsupervised SAR change detection with despeckling autoencoders
abstract: Change detection is an outstanding topic in remote sensing due to its many civilian and military applications. Methods based on Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imaging have become popular in recent years because of the ability of SAR sensors to operate in all-weather, day-and-night conditions. However, due to the nature of SAR images, speckle perturbation leads to high false alarm rates in change detection schemes. We propose in this paper a new approach based on unsupervised representation learning. We first extend the popular denoising autoencoders framework to account for speckle fluctuations and obtain a new feature space robust to multiplicative Gamma noise. Afterwards, the change detection map can be computed in this representation space and then, projected back to the original image domain. Experiments in very high resolution SAR images illustrate the performances of the proposed strategy.

articleTitle: Experimental UAV detection using 4G-LTE-based passive Radar
abstract: This paper presents detection results of drone in a passive radar framework, that exploits 4G Long Term Evolution signals. The results are based on an experiment using a non-cooperative transmitter. The processing of the data is described, in particular how general passive algorithm can be adjusted to the processing of LTE signals. The results are then discussed.

articleTitle: Results of Dual-Polarimetric Airborne Passive Radar
abstract: Polarimetry in remote sensing applications has emerged as a valuable technique for enhancing the information content of Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) images. Passive radar exploits existing illuminators of opportunity, e.g. broadcast or communication transmitters, for sensing applications, i.e. target detection or SAR imaging. Terrestrial broadcast transmitters emit the signal typically using only one linear polarization (horizontal or vertical). In this cases, full-polarimetry, as it is known from active remote sensing applications, is not usable for passive radar. However, if the receiver is equipped with dual-polarized antenna elements, dual-polarimetry techniques can be applied. It has the potential to improve the quality and interpretability of passive radar data. In this paper, we present results and analysis of dual-polarimetric passive SAR images. We calculate the coherence between horizontal and vertical polarized SAR images for two different scenes. Additionally, we calculate the Stokes parameter and derive a quantitative measure from the Stokes parameters to improve the interpretability of the SAR images.

articleTitle: Sequential Multi-model Unscented Kalman Filter for Shipborne High Frequency Surface Wave Radar
abstract: Shipborne high frequency surface wave radar (HFSWR) is a development of HFSWR, which install the transmitting and receiving equipment on the ship. In tracking problem, existing shipborne HFSWR are typically centered on the shipborne platform for detection and transferred to a coordinate system with a fixed origin. Therefore, the accuracy of the measurement on the shipborne platform is critical. However, in practice, it is a challenge to determine the accuracy of shipborne platform information measurements, which can lead to a reduction in the accuracy oftarget condition estimates. In this paper, we propose a sequential multi-model unscented Kalman filter (SMUKF) to address the uncertainty in the measurement of the shipborne platform. The SMUKF can get thejoint state estimation of shipborne platforms and targets. By applying multi-model method and using a more accurate filter value in the traceless Kalman filter, the SMUKF fuses the multi-model output to mitigate the impact of measurement errors on the target state estimation accuracy. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed SMUKF outperforms the unscented Kalman filter (UKF) in terms of state estimation accuracy, and is more suitable for shipborne HFSWR.

articleTitle: Enhanced Maximum Interelement Constrained Array Design via Simple Hole-Filling Strategy
abstract: In this paper, we propose a new sparse array design via the maximum interelement spacing constraint (MISC) criterion. The array, called enhanced MISC array (xMISC), is developed by filling the holes in the conventional improved MISC array (IMISC). First, the hole locations in the IMISC array are analyzed, then a simplified hole-filling strategy is proposed. Compared to the existing MISC and IMISC arrays, the xMISC array exhibits enhanced uniform degrees of freedom (uDOF) and relatively reduced mutual coupling. Besides, the xMISC retains a hole-free difference co-array. Moreover, the closed-form expressions for sensor locations, weight functions, and achievable DOF are derived in detail. Numerical examples validated the merits of the xMISC array.

articleTitle: A clutter suppression method based on the intrinsic mode functions reconstruction and information geometry space detection
abstract: In this paper, we applied a clutter suppression method based on the complex empirical mode decomposition (CEMD), which by screening the intrinsic mode functions (IMFs) to reconstruct signal for clutter suppression. The data before and after clutter suppression is processed using the information geometry method and calculating the geometry distance between center cell with the neighboring cell. Simulation results verified that by comparing the information geometry before clutter suppression, the number of false targets and false alarm probability reduce by combining CEMD and information geometry method in the clutter background. And the detection probability is improved effectively after clutter suppression with CEMD.

articleTitle: Noise Elimination with Compressive Sensing in Pulse Doppler Radar Receivers
abstract: Compressive sensing (CS) is an attractive well-known technique used to reconstruct sparse signals with much fewer samples than Nyquist rate samples. However, when the signal-to-noise ratio is relatively low, the target’s detection sensitivity degrades. In this study, we propose a noise elimination method of CS reconstructed signals that utilizes the difference of the pulse-to-pulse correlation between the target and noise components, and it is termed “NewCS.” Monte Carlo simulations to evaluate the false alarm probability and probability of detection characteristics verified the effectiveness of the method. In a typical case, the sensitivity improvement over the conventional pulse Doppler radar without CS was greater than 3 dB at a compression ratio of 1.

articleTitle: Large Baseline Bistatic Radar Imaging for Space Domain Awareness
abstract: Bistatic radars with long baselines are gaining popularity due to the increased interest in Space Domain Awareness, but require significant investment due to the need for large antenna apertures, low noise temperatures, and synchronized clocks. However, radio telescopes can be paired with high-power radars to create long baseline bistatic-multistatic radar networks. This paper describes novel long baseline bistatic measurements using the Millstone Hill Radar (MHR) in the USA and receivers in multiple antennas of the e-MERLIN array in the United Kingdom and the Westerbork Synthesis Radio Telescope (WSRT) in the Netherlands. When provided with basic information about the transmitted waveform, multiple receivers can detect, identify, and track multiple targets. The paper also presents a framework for imaging tumbling targets, demonstrating its effectiveness on real data collected by a novel system concept. This framework integrates coherent integration and Doppler processing techniques to improve signal-to-noise ratio, estimate and correct target motion, and estimate the rotation period and dimensions of tumbling targets, resulting in a clear image of the space object. The presented framework and the proposed system concept have potential to improve bistatic imaging, leading to better characterization of objects in Earth orbits undergoing complex motion, with significant implications for applications such as space domain awareness, space traffic management, and space object characterization.

articleTitle: Realistic Scatterer Based Adversarial Attacks on SAR Image Classifiers
abstract: Adversarial attacks have highlighted the vulnerability of classifiers based on machine learning for Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) Automatic Target Recognition (ATR) tasks. An adversarial attack perturbs SAR images of on-ground targets such that the classifiers are misled into making incorrect predictions. However, many existing attacking techniques rely on arbitrary manipulation of SAR images while overlooking the feasibility of executing the attacks on real-world SAR imagery. Instead, adversarial attacks should be able to be implemented by physical actions, for example, placing additional false objects as scatterers around the on-ground target to perturb the SAR image and fool the SAR ATR.In this paper, we propose the On-Target Scatterer Attack (OTSA), a scatterer-based physical adversarial attack. To ensure the feasibility of its physical execution, we enforce a constraint on the positioning of the scatterers. Specifically, we restrict the scatterers to be placed only on the target instead of in the shadow regions or the background. To achieve this, we introduce a positioning score based on Gaussian kernels and formulate an optimization problem for our OTSA attack. Using a gradient ascent method to solve the optimization problem, the OTSA can generate a vector of parameters describing the positions, shapes, sizes and amplitudes of the scatterers to guide the physical execution of the attack that will mislead SAR image classifiers. The experimental results show that our attack obtains significantly higher success rates under the positioning constraint compared with the existing method.

articleTitle: Decentralized Digital Clock Drift Compensation in Distributed Radar Sensor Networks Through Single-Tone Frequency Broadcasts
abstract: This paper presents a decentralized broadcast technique for estimating the clock drift of platforms cooperating in a distributed radar sensor network for the purpose of achieving frequency, phase, and time synchronization. The proposed method is advantageous for existing digital radar systems as it can be implemented entirely in software without the use of additional RF hardware required by other frequency synchronization techniques. The signal model for signals transmitted and received in various clock domains is presented to highlight the impact of clock drift on signal transfers and an estimation model is subsequently derived for estimating and correcting the clock drifts on each platform. A modified version of a previously developed phase and clock bias correction procedure is outlined for correcting time and phase after the frequency synchronization is completed. The technique is validated in simulation and results are demonstrated showing the clock drift estimation accuracy as a function of signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), carrier frequency, and network size, as well as a comparison in bias estimation to the drift-free case assumed by other techniques.

articleTitle: DoA techniques in UAV detection with DVB-T based Passive Radar
abstract: In this paper, the study of different target Direction of Arrival (DoA) techniques for Passive Radar (PR) exploiting Digital Video Broadcasting signals is carried out. Conventional Beamforming (CBF) algorithms based on signal covariance matrix estimation are compared to Amplitude-Comparison (ACM) and Phase-Comparison (PCM) monopulse techniques to find the solution that provides higher accuracy for Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAV) detection and localization. DoA algorithms were performed in the transformed domain defined by the cross ambiguity function, and were evaluated using real radar data acquired by a PR demonstrator developed at the University of Alcalá, which used a Uniform Linear Array (ULA) in the surveillance channel. CBF techniques were designed considering the whole ULA, whereas monopulse ones were implemented using a reduced sub-array. Results proved that ACM and PCM are suitable for target angle of arrival estimation in PR systems. However, CBF techniques provide higher estimation accuracy, being the proper DoA estimation method of those studied for UAV localization in PR scenarios.

articleTitle: Coherency limits and synchronisation of a netted radar system using USRPs as nodes
abstract: This paper intends to further evaluate the synchronisation capabilities of multiple networked USRPs. We obtained a priori knowledge of the USRP’s coherency limits between daughterboards within a single device and presented such results in our previous work [1]. The final aim of this work is to build a versatile networked radar system which may take advantage of the transceiver capabilities of its different nodes to form a multistatic radar. At the expense of high complexity, multistatic radar systems exploit spatial diversity to increase the probability of detection and tracking of targets. To properly make use of these advantages, the involved nodes must agree on a common time base $({t}_{0})$. A succession of precisely timed events must occur, as to maximise the resulting SNR on the measurement side. In this paper, a customized software network time protocol (NTP) server is added between the control computers and it is combined with crontab as to timely start the transmitting and sampling sequences on the different nodes. Up-chirp and sinusoid waveforms were used for measuring the offset with ${t}_{0}$ and for evaluating the achievable coherency limits. Thus, by evaluating different synchronisation methods (analogue and digital), fractional frequency of $2.8{\cdot }{10}^{-13}$ and phase noise of −118 dBc/Hz at 10 Hz frequency offset were measured.

articleTitle: Radar Multi Object Tracking using DNN Features
abstract: A single frame radar-based multi-object tracker that aims to improve data association for better tracking performance is proposed. Firstly, a baseline tracker based on track-by-detection paradigm was implemented for automotive radar. Secondly, investigation on the performance of the tracker when tracking individual classes separately versus all classes together was performed. Thirdly, appearance features were extracted from a neural network and added as an additional metric to the cost matrix for improved data association. Extensive experiments on the 2D RadarScenes dataset and a 3D proprietary Lunewave dataset (in partnership with NXP Semiconductors) showed a consistent improvement in the tracking performance using the approach proposed by adding features extracted from a neural network.

articleTitle: Concept for an Automatic Annotation of Automotive Radar Data Using AI-segmented Aerial Camera Images
abstract: This paper presents an approach to automatically annotate automotive radar data with AI-segmented aerial camera images. For this, the images of an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) above a radar vehicle are panoptically segmented and mapped in the ground plane onto the radar images. The detected instances and segments in the camera image can then be applied directly as labels for the radar data. Owing to the advantageous bird’s eye position, the UAV camera does not suffer from optical occlusion and is capable of creating annotations within the complete field of view of the radar. The effectiveness and scalability are demonstrated in measurements, where 589 pedestrians in the radar data were automatically labeled within 2 minutes.

articleTitle: End-to-End Training of Neural Networks for Automotive Radar Interference Mitigation
abstract: In this paper we propose a new method for training neural networks (NNs) for frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radar mutual interference mitigation. Instead of training NNs to regress from interfered to clean radar signals as in previous work, we train NNs directly on object detection maps. We do so by performing a continuous relaxation of the cell-averaging constant false alarm rate (CA-CFAR) peak detector, which is a well-established algorithm for object detection using radar. With this new training objective we are able to increase object detection performance by a large margin. Furthermore, we introduce separable convolution kernels to strongly reduce the number of parameters and computational complexity of convolutional NN architectures for radar applications. We validate our contributions with experiments on real-world measurement data and compare them against signal processing interference mitigation methods.

articleTitle: Track-Before-Detect Adaptive Birth Using Generic Observation Model Labeled Random Finite Sets
